    current_schema_txn: LazySchemaTransaction | None,
    normalized_tables: tuple[SqlTableName, ...],
) -> LazyResult[BootstrapScopeExistsMap | None]:
    from l2000_connection.schema_transaction import _schema_static_value_lazy

    if current_schema_txn is None:
        from l3200_metadata.bootstrap_state import BootstrapPlanningError

        msg = "schema-transaction bootstrap evidence requires a ServerPlan-owning schema transaction"
        raise BootstrapPlanningError(msg)
    results, unknown_tables = _schema_transaction_projected_table_evidence(
        current_schema_txn,
        normalized_tables,
    )
    if unknown_tables:
        batch_results = current_schema_txn.table_exists_many_for_schema_batch_lazy(
            tuple(unknown_tables),
        )

        def _merge_batch(
            batch: BootstrapScopeExistsMap,
        ) -> BootstrapScopeExistsMap | None:
            return _merge_schema_batch_table_evidence(
                results,
                tuple(unknown_tables),
                batch,
            )

        merged: LazyResult[BootstrapScopeExistsMap | None] = batch_results.map(
            _merge_batch,
        )
        return merged
    return _schema_static_value_lazy(current_schema_txn, results)

class _ManagedTableExistsCache:
    """Connection-local table-exists cache registered with the cache manager."""

    def __init__(self: _ManagedTableExistsCache, connection_id: ConnectionId) -> None:
        self._cache = LocalMetadataCache[bool](
            name=f"table_exists:{connection_id}",
            invalidation_policy=LocalMetadataInvalidationPolicy.SCHEMA_GENERATION,
        )
        self._keys: set[str] = set()

    def get(self: _ManagedTableExistsCache, table_name: SqlTableName) -> bool | None:
        normalized_table_name = str(table_name)
        value = self._cache.get(normalized_table_name)
        if value is None:
            self._keys.discard(normalized_table_name)
        cached_value: bool | None = value
        return cached_value

    def set(self: _ManagedTableExistsCache, table_name: SqlTableName, exists: bool) -> None:
        normalized_table_name = str(table_name)
        self._keys.add(normalized_table_name)
        self._cache.set(
            normalized_table_name,
            exists,
            tags=[schema_global_tag(), schema_table_tag(SqlTableName(normalized_table_name))],
        )

    def set_many(
        self: _ManagedTableExistsCache,
        facts: Sequence[tuple[SqlTableName, bool]],
    ) -> None:
        """Record authoritative table facts with one managed-cache mutation."""

        normalized = tuple((str(table_name), exists) for table_name, exists in facts)
        self._keys.update(table_name for table_name, _exists in normalized)
        # This cache uses SCHEMA_GENERATION invalidation, which clears the
        # complete connection-local cache on a generation event. Per-key tag
        # metadata would duplicate that ownership for every table.
        self._cache.set_many_values(normalized)

    def seal_snapshot(self: _ManagedTableExistsCache) -> None:
        """Expire the completeness proof with the managed table facts."""
        self._cache.set(_sealed_table_snapshot_key, True)

    def has_current_sealed_snapshot(self: _ManagedTableExistsCache) -> bool:
        """Report whether cache invalidation preserved the completeness proof."""
        return self._cache.get(_sealed_table_snapshot_key) is True

    def clear(self: _ManagedTableExistsCache) -> None:
        self._keys.clear()
        self._cache.clear()

    def pop(self: _ManagedTableExistsCache, table_name: SqlTableName, default: object = None) -> bool | object:
        normalized_table_name = str(table_name)
        self._keys.discard(normalized_table_name)
        value = self._cache.get(normalized_table_name)
        self._cache.delete(normalized_table_name)
        return default if value is None else value

    def items(self: _ManagedTableExistsCache) -> tuple[tuple[SqlTableName, bool], ...]:
        values: list[tuple[SqlTableName, bool]] = []
        for table_name in tuple(self._keys):
            value = self.get(SqlTableName(table_name))
            if value is not None:
                values.append((SqlTableName(table_name), value))
        return tuple(values)

    def __contains__(self: _ManagedTableExistsCache, table_name: object) -> bool:
        return type(table_name) is str and self.get(SqlTableName(table_name)) is not None

    def __getitem__(self: _ManagedTableExistsCache, table_name: SqlTableName) -> bool:
        value = self.get(table_name)
        if value is None:
            raise KeyError(table_name)
        return value

    def __setitem__(self: _ManagedTableExistsCache, table_name: SqlTableName, exists: bool) -> None:
        self.set(table_name, exists)

    def __len__(self: _ManagedTableExistsCache) -> int:
        return len(self.items())

class _ConnectionTableCacheMixin:
    """Table-existence, bootstrap-scope, column, and index caches."""

    if TYPE_CHECKING:
        _authoritative_template_existing_tables: frozenset[SqlTableName] | None
        _authoritative_planning_catalog_contract: PlanningCatalogContract | None
        _authoritative_planning_catalog_models: tuple[type[DatabaseObjectRow], ...] | None
        _authoritative_planning_catalog_sealed: bool
        _authoritative_planning_catalog_evolution_allowed: bool
        _bootstrap_column_proof_cache: BootstrapColumnProofCache
        _bootstrap_scope_facts_by_key: dict[BootstrapAuthorityKey, BootstrapFactsHash]
        _bootstrap_scope_keys_by_table: dict[SqlTableName, set[BootstrapAuthorityKey]]
        _bootstrap_scope_proof_cache: dict[BootstrapAuthorityKey, BootstrapScopeProof]
        _bootstrap_scope_tables_by_key: dict[BootstrapAuthorityKey, set[SqlTableName]]
        _bootstrap_seed_fact_hashes: dict[BootstrapSeedFactKey, BootstrapFactsHash]
        _column_cache: SchemaColumnCache
        _invalidate_column_cache: Callable[[SqlTableName], None]
        _known_absent_schema_tables: KnownAbsentSchemaTables
        _log_planning_models_by_table: tuple[tuple[SqlTableName, type[DatabaseObjectRow]], ...]
        _verified_bootstrap_scopes: set[BootstrapAuthorityKey]
        _planning_catalog_snapshot: PlanningCatalog | None
        _planning_catalog_model_overlay: PlanningCatalogOverlay | None
        _planning_catalog_model_overlay_base_id: int | None
        _table_exists_cache: _ManagedTableExistsCache
        _table_exists_cache_sealed: bool
        _cached_existing_tables: Callable[[], tuple[SqlTableName, ...]]

    _planning_catalog_snapshot_key: PlanningCatalogCacheKey | None

    def _table_exists_uncached(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName) -> bool:
        """Backend-specific table existence check (uncached).

        Subclasses must implement this to perform the actual database query.
        Application code should call ``table_exists()`` instead, which provides caching.

        Args:
            table_name: The name of the table to check.

        Returns:
            True if the table exists, False otherwise.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    async def _table_exists_uncached_async(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName) -> bool:
        """Async backend-specific table existence check (uncached).

        Async variant of :meth:`_table_exists_uncached`. Subclasses must
        implement this using their native async driver so that the event loop
        is not blocked and thread affinity is preserved.

        Args:
            table_name: The name of the table to check.

        Returns:
            True if the table exists, False otherwise.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    @pure_lazy
    def _table_exists_from_cache(
        self: Self,
        table_name: SqlTableName,
    ) -> bool | None:
        """Check the table existence cache, returning None on cache miss.

        Shared by :meth:`table_exists` and :meth:`table_exists_async` to avoid
        duplicating the cache-check and sealed-cache logic.

        Returns:
            True/False if the answer is cached (or cache is sealed), or None
            if a database query is needed.
        """
        cached_value = self._table_exists_cache.get(table_name)
        if cached_value is not None:
            return cached_value
        if _ConnectionTableCacheMixin.is_table_exists_cache_sealed(self):
            return False
        return None

    def bootstrap_column_proof_snapshot(
        self: Self,
        table_name: SqlTableName,
    ) -> frozenset[SqlColumnName] | None:
        """Return connection-proven bootstrap columns for ``table_name``."""
        proof_columns = self._bootstrap_column_proof_cache.get(table_name)
        if type(proof_columns) is not frozenset:
            return None
        return frozenset(SqlColumnName(column_name) for column_name in proof_columns)

    @pure_lazy
    def proven_existing_table_snapshot(self: Self) -> frozenset[SqlTableName] | None:
        """Return connection-local table facts without probing the backend."""
        proven_tables: set[SqlTableName] = set()
        authoritative_existing_tables = self._authoritative_template_existing_tables
        if type(authoritative_existing_tables) is frozenset:
            proven_tables.update(SqlTableName(table_name) for table_name in authoritative_existing_tables)
        proven_tables.update(SqlTableName(table_name) for table_name, exists in self._table_exists_cache.items() if exists is True)
        if not proven_tables:
            return None
        return frozenset(proven_tables)

    def bootstrap_ddl_lockdown_table_presence(self: Self) -> bool | None:
        """Return cached DDL-lockdown table presence when connection facts prove it."""
        lockdown_table = SqlTableName("sys_ddl_lockdown")
        if lockdown_table in self._known_absent_schema_tables:
            return False
        authoritative_existing_tables = self._authoritative_template_existing_tables
        if type(authoritative_existing_tables) is frozenset:
            return lockdown_table in authoritative_existing_tables
        cached_presence = self._table_exists_from_cache(lockdown_table)
        return cached_presence

    def accepts_bootstrap_planning_model_evolution(self: Self) -> bool:
        """Return whether bootstrap may extend the connection's model catalog."""
        return self._authoritative_planning_catalog_models is None or self._authoritative_planning_catalog_evolution_allowed

    def _bind_log_planning_model(
        self: Self,
        table_name: SqlTableName,
        model: type[DatabaseObjectRow],
    ) -> None:
        """Bind the exact generated log model used by this connection."""
        models_by_table = dict(self._log_planning_models_by_table)
        models_by_table[table_name] = model
        self._log_planning_models_by_table = tuple(sorted(models_by_table.items()))

    def _planning_log_models(self: Self) -> tuple[type[DatabaseObjectRow], ...]:
        """Return connection-owned generated log-model facts."""
        return tuple(model for _table_name, model in self._log_planning_models_by_table)

    def bind_planning_models(self: Self, *models: type[DatabaseObjectRow]) -> None:
        """Bind an explicit model set at a connection bootstrap boundary."""
        existing_models = self._authoritative_planning_catalog_models or ()
        bound_models = tuple(dict.fromkeys((*existing_models, *models)))
        existing_contract = self._authoritative_planning_catalog_contract
        sealed_contract = self._authoritative_planning_catalog_sealed and not self._authoritative_planning_catalog_evolution_allowed
        if existing_contract is not None and sealed_contract:
            existing_contract.require_subset(bound_models)
            contract = existing_contract
        else:
            contract = PlanningCatalogContract.from_models(bound_models)
        self.bind_authoritative_planning_catalog(
            contract,
            bound_models,
            allow_schema_evolution=self._authoritative_planning_catalog_evolution_allowed,
            sealed=sealed_contract,
        )

    def bind_authoritative_planning_catalog(
        self: Self,
        contract: PlanningCatalogContract,
        models: Sequence[type[DatabaseObjectRow]],
        *,
        allow_schema_evolution: bool,
        sealed: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        """Bind exact template authority and invalidate earlier catalog products."""
        contract.require_subset(models)
        self._authoritative_planning_catalog_contract = contract
        self._authoritative_planning_catalog_models = tuple(models)
        self._authoritative_planning_catalog_evolution_allowed = allow_schema_evolution
        self._authoritative_planning_catalog_sealed = sealed
        self._planning_catalog_snapshot = None
        self._planning_catalog_snapshot_key = None
        self._planning_catalog_model_overlay = None
        self._planning_catalog_model_overlay_base_id = None

    def planning_catalog_models(self: Self) -> tuple[type[DatabaseObjectRow], ...] | None:
        """Return the exact connection-bound model set without global discovery."""
        models = self._authoritative_planning_catalog_models
        if models is None:
            return None
        contract = self._authoritative_planning_catalog_contract
        if contract is None:
            msg = "Sealed template connection has no authoritative planning catalog contract"
            raise RuntimeError(msg)
        return models or None

    def planning_catalog_cache_key(
        self: Self,
        backend_type: BackendType,
    ) -> PlanningCatalogCacheKey | None:
        """Return a stable connection-local planning-catalog cache key."""
        if not self.is_table_exists_cache_sealed():
            return None
        proven_tables = tuple(sorted(self._cached_existing_tables()))
        if not proven_tables:
            return None
        contract = self._authoritative_planning_catalog_contract
        if contract is None:
            msg = "Sealed template connection has no authoritative planning catalog contract"
            raise RuntimeError(msg)
        return PlanningCatalogCacheKey(
            "sealed",
            backend_type,
            (
                *(PlanningCatalogEvidenceToken(table_name) for table_name in proven_tables),
                PlanningCatalogEvidenceToken(f"catalog:{contract.digest()}"),
                PlanningCatalogEvidenceToken(f"evolution:{self._authoritative_planning_catalog_evolution_allowed}"),
            ),
        )

    def get_planning_catalog_snapshot(
        self: Self,
        cache_key: PlanningCatalogCacheKey,
    ) -> PlanningCatalog | None:
        """Return a cached planning catalog snapshot for ``cache_key``."""
        if self._planning_catalog_snapshot_key != cache_key:
            return None
        return self._planning_catalog_snapshot

        overlay = self._planning_catalog_model_overlay
        overlay_base_id = self._planning_catalog_model_overlay_base_id
        if overlay is None or overlay_base_id != id(base_catalog):

    def set_planning_catalog_model_overlay(

    def _record_table_exists_result(

    def _record_table_exists_result_lazy(

    @pure_lazy
    def _validate_table_exists_args(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName) -> None:
        """Validate table_name argument (shared by table_exists/table_exists_async)."""
        if not table_name:
            msg = "table_name must be a non-empty string"
            raise ValueError(msg)

    @pure_lazy
    def _table_exists_uncached_under_authority_lazy(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName) -> LazyResult[bool]:
        """Async single-table physical existence probe under schema/capability authority."""
        with _imp_impl_l2070_execution_context().server_plan_execution_context():
            return _require_lazy_table_existence_owner(self)._table_exists_uncached_lazy(
                table_name,
            )

    @pure_lazy
    def table_exists_lazy(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName) -> LazyResult[bool]:
        """Check if a table exists in the database (cached), async variant.

        Async variant of :meth:`table_exists`. Uses the same in-memory cache
        and calls :meth:`_table_exists_uncached_async` on cache miss.

        Args:
            table_name: The name of the table to check.

        Returns:
            True if the table exists, False otherwise.

        Raises:
            db_exc.OperationalError: If an error occurs during the check.
        """
        self._validate_table_exists_args(table_name)
        cached = self._table_exists_from_cache(table_name)
        if cached is not None:
            return LazyResult.of(bool(cached))
        msg = (
            "Lazy table existence requires observed schema facts or cached projected state; "
            "unknown table existence cannot probe physical schema through table_exists_lazy()."
        )
        raise LazyPurityError(msg)

    def invalidate_table_exists_cache(
        self: Self,
        table_name: SqlTableName | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Invalidate table existence cache.

        Call this when schema changes outside of normal ``create_table_from_schema()``
        operations (e.g., manual DDL, migrations, or testing).

        If the cache is sealed, this automatically unseals it because invalidation
        implies the cached state may no longer be accurate.

        Args:
            table_name: Specific table to invalidate. If None, clears entire cache.
        """
        self._invalidate_table_exists_cache_direct(UNSET if table_name is None else SqlTableName(table_name))

    def _invalidate_table_exists_cache_direct(
        self: Self,
        table_name: SqlTableName | Unset = UNSET,
    ) -> None:
        """Invalidate table-existence cache from an authorized eager boundary."""
        # Unseal if sealed - invalidation means cached state is unreliable
        if self._table_exists_cache_sealed:
            self._table_exists_cache_sealed = False
        from l2055_lazy_result.purity import bootstrap_lifecycle_effect_boundary_lazy, in_lazy_context

        normalized_table_name = SqlTableName(table_name) if table_name is not UNSET else None
        invalidated_tables = (normalized_table_name,) if normalized_table_name is not None else ()
        if in_lazy_context():
            with bootstrap_lifecycle_effect_boundary_lazy():
                self.invalidate_bootstrap_scope_verification(
                    table_names=invalidated_tables,
                )
        else:
            self.invalidate_bootstrap_scope_verification(
                table_names=invalidated_tables,
            )

        if table_name is UNSET:
            self._table_exists_cache.clear()
        else:
            assert normalized_table_name is not None
            self._table_exists_cache.pop(normalized_table_name, None)
        if table_name is UNSET:
            self._planning_catalog_snapshot = None
            self._planning_catalog_snapshot_key = None
            self._planning_catalog_model_overlay = None
            self._planning_catalog_model_overlay_base_id = None
        known_absent_schema_tables = self._known_absent_schema_tables
        if table_name is UNSET:
            known_absent_schema_tables.clear()
        else:
            known_absent_schema_tables.discard(SqlTableName(table_name))

    @pure_lazy
    def is_bootstrap_scope_verified(
        self: Self,
        verification_key: BootstrapAuthorityKey,
    ) -> bool:
        """Return whether the caller already proved a bootstrap invariant."""
        return verification_key in self._verified_bootstrap_scopes

    def cache_bootstrap_scope_proof(
        self: Self,
        proof: BootstrapScopeProof,
    ) -> None:
        """Cache a non-authoritative bootstrap proof for the current connection."""
        verification_key = proof.verification_key
        if verification_key == NO_BOOTSTRAP_SCOPE_VERIFICATION_KEY:
            return
        assert type(verification_key) is BootstrapScopeVerificationKey
        proof_cache = self._bootstrap_scope_proof_cache
        proof_cache[BootstrapAuthorityKey(verification_key)] = proof

    def clear_bootstrap_scope_proof(
        self: Self,
        verification_key: BootstrapAuthorityKey | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Drop cached bootstrap-scope proofs for this connection."""
        proof_cache = self._bootstrap_scope_proof_cache
        if verification_key is None:
            proof_cache.clear()
            return
        proof_cache.pop(verification_key, None)

    def mark_bootstrap_scope_verified(
        self: Self,
        verification_key: BootstrapAuthorityKey,
        *,
        table_names: Sequence[SqlTableName] = (),
        facts_hash: BootstrapFactsHash | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Record a bootstrap invariant as proven for this connection."""
        self._verified_bootstrap_scopes.add(verification_key)
        self.clear_bootstrap_scope_proof(verification_key)
        previous_tables = self._bootstrap_scope_tables_by_key.pop(verification_key, set())
        for table_name in previous_tables:
            table_keys = self._bootstrap_scope_keys_by_table.get(table_name)
            if table_keys is not None:
                table_keys.discard(verification_key)
                if not table_keys:
                    self._bootstrap_scope_keys_by_table.pop(table_name, None)
        normalized_table_names = {SqlTableName(table_name) for table_name in table_names if str(table_name)}
        if normalized_table_names:
            self._bootstrap_scope_tables_by_key[verification_key] = normalized_table_names
            for table_name in normalized_table_names:
                self._bootstrap_scope_keys_by_table.setdefault(table_name, set()).add(verification_key)
        for table_name in normalized_table_names:
            self._record_table_exists_result(SqlTableName(table_name), True)
        if facts_hash:
            self._bootstrap_scope_facts_by_key[verification_key] = facts_hash
        else:
            self._bootstrap_scope_facts_by_key.pop(verification_key, None)

    def verified_bootstrap_scope_fact_for_tables(
        self: Self,
        table_names: Sequence[SqlTableName],
    ) -> BootstrapFactsHash | None:
        """Return a durable fact hash for an exactly matching verified table scope."""
        normalized_table_names = {SqlTableName(table_name) for table_name in table_names if str(table_name)}
        if not normalized_table_names:
            return None
        for scope_key in self._verified_bootstrap_scopes:
            if self._bootstrap_scope_tables_by_key.get(scope_key) == normalized_table_names:
                facts_hash = self._bootstrap_scope_facts_by_key.get(scope_key)
                return BootstrapFactsHash(facts_hash) if facts_hash is not None else None
        table_fact_pairs: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        for table_name in sorted(normalized_table_names):
            scope_key = BootstrapAuthorityKey(f"schema-table:{table_name}")
            facts_hash = self._bootstrap_scope_facts_by_key.get(scope_key)
            if scope_key not in self._verified_bootstrap_scopes or facts_hash is None:
                return None
            table_fact_pairs.append((str(scope_key), str(facts_hash)))
        return BootstrapFactsHash(sha256(repr(tuple(table_fact_pairs)).encode()).hexdigest())

    def invalidate_bootstrap_scope_verification(
        self: Self,
        verification_key: BootstrapAuthorityKey | None = None,
        *,
        table_names: Sequence[SqlTableName] = (),
    ) -> None:
        """Invalidate optimistic bootstrap assumptions after schema changes."""
        from l2055_lazy_result.purity import (
            LazyPurityError,
            in_bootstrap_schema_write_boundary,
            in_lazy_context,
        )

        if in_lazy_context() and not in_bootstrap_schema_write_boundary():
            msg = "invalidate_bootstrap_scope_verification() cannot mutate connection caches during lazy planning"
            raise LazyPurityError(msg)
        normalized_table_names = {SqlTableName(table_name) for table_name in table_names if str(table_name)}
        if verification_key is not None:
            self.clear_bootstrap_scope_proof(verification_key)
            self._verified_bootstrap_scopes.discard(verification_key)
            self._bootstrap_scope_facts_by_key.pop(verification_key, None)
            previous_tables = self._bootstrap_scope_tables_by_key.pop(verification_key, set())
            for table_name in previous_tables:
                table_keys = self._bootstrap_scope_keys_by_table.get(table_name)
                if table_keys is not None:
                    table_keys.discard(verification_key)
                    if not table_keys:
                        self._bootstrap_scope_keys_by_table.pop(table_name, None)
            return
        if normalized_table_names:
            invalidated_keys = {
                verification_key
                for table_name in normalized_table_names
                for verification_key in self._bootstrap_scope_keys_by_table.get(table_name, set())
            }
            for current_key in invalidated_keys:
                self.invalidate_bootstrap_scope_verification(BootstrapAuthorityKey(current_key))
            return
        self.clear_bootstrap_scope_proof()
        self._verified_bootstrap_scopes.clear()
        self._bootstrap_scope_tables_by_key.clear()
        self._bootstrap_scope_keys_by_table.clear()
        self._bootstrap_seed_fact_hashes.clear()
        self._bootstrap_scope_facts_by_key.clear()

    def bootstrap_seed_fact_matches(
        self: Self,
        seed_fact_key: BootstrapSeedFactKey,
        seed_fact_hash: BootstrapFactsHash,
    ) -> bool:
        """Return whether a deterministic bootstrap seed fact is already proven."""
        return self._bootstrap_seed_fact_hashes.get(seed_fact_key) == seed_fact_hash

    def bootstrap_scope_fact_matches(
        self: Self,
        verification_key: BootstrapAuthorityKey,
        facts_hash: BootstrapFactsHash,
    ) -> bool:
        """Return whether a bootstrap scope was proven with a matching fact hash."""
        return self._bootstrap_scope_facts_by_key.get(verification_key) == facts_hash

    def mark_bootstrap_seed_fact_verified(
        self: Self,
        seed_fact_key: BootstrapSeedFactKey,
        seed_fact_hash: BootstrapFactsHash,
    ) -> None:
        """Record a deterministic bootstrap seed fact as proven for this connection."""
        if seed_fact_key and seed_fact_hash:
            self._bootstrap_seed_fact_hashes[seed_fact_key] = seed_fact_hash

    @pure_lazy
    def _bootstrap_seed_fact_proof(
        self: Self,
        proof: BootstrapScopeProof | Unset = UNSET,
    ) -> Mapping[BootstrapSeedFactKey, BootstrapFactsHash]:
        seed_fact_hashes = dict(self._bootstrap_seed_fact_hashes)

        if proof is not UNSET:
            seed_fact_hashes.update(
                (BootstrapSeedFactKey(seed_key), BootstrapFactsHash(seed_hash)) for seed_key, seed_hash in proof.seed_fact_hashes.items()
            )

        return seed_fact_hashes

    def seed_bootstrap_proof(
        self: Self,
        *,
        verification_keys: BootstrapVerificationKeys = (),
        scope_tables_by_key: BootstrapScopeTables | None = None,
        existing_tables: Sequence[SqlTableName] = (),
        verified_bootstrap_tables: Sequence[SqlTableName] = (),
        verified_domain_bootstrap_tables: Sequence[SqlTableName] = (),
        seed_fact_hashes: BootstrapSeedFactHashInput | None = None,
        scope_facts_by_key: BootstrapScopeFactInput | None = None,
        columns_by_table: BootstrapColumnProofInput | None = None,
        bootstrap_system_session_verified: bool = False,
        table_exists_cache_sealed: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Stamp authoritative bootstrap state onto this connection."""
        normalized_existing_tables = tuple(dict.fromkeys(SqlTableName(table_name) for table_name in existing_tables if str(table_name)))
        normalized_verification_keys = {
            BootstrapAuthorityKey(verification_key) for verification_key in verification_keys if str(verification_key)
        }
        normalized_bootstrap_tables = {str(table_name) for table_name in verified_bootstrap_tables if str(table_name)}
        normalized_domain_tables = {str(table_name) for table_name in verified_domain_bootstrap_tables if str(table_name)}
        normalized_seed_fact_hashes = {
            BootstrapSeedFactKey(scope_key): BootstrapFactsHash(fact_hash)
            for scope_key, fact_hash in (seed_fact_hashes or {}).items()
            if str(scope_key) and str(fact_hash)
        }
        normalized_scope_facts = {
            BootstrapAuthorityKey(scope_key): BootstrapFactsHash(fact_hash)
            for scope_key, fact_hash in (scope_facts_by_key or {}).items()
            if str(scope_key) and str(fact_hash)
        }
        normalized_columns_by_table: dict[
            SqlTableName,
            frozenset[SqlColumnName],
        ] = {
            SqlTableName(table_name): frozenset(SqlColumnName(column_name) for column_name in column_names if str(column_name))
            for table_name, column_names in (columns_by_table or {}).items()
            if str(table_name)
        }

        self._verified_bootstrap_scopes = normalized_verification_keys
        self._bootstrap_column_proof_cache = BootstrapColumnProofCache(normalized_columns_by_table)
        self.clear_bootstrap_scope_proof()
        self._bootstrap_scope_tables_by_key.clear()
        self._bootstrap_scope_keys_by_table.clear()
        self._bootstrap_seed_fact_hashes = normalized_seed_fact_hashes
        self._bootstrap_scope_facts_by_key = {
            scope_key: fact_hash for scope_key, fact_hash in normalized_scope_facts.items() if scope_key in normalized_verification_keys
        }
        if scope_tables_by_key is not None:
            for verification_key in normalized_verification_keys:
                table_names = {
                    SqlTableName(table_name)
                    for table_name in scope_tables_by_key.get(BootstrapAuthorityKey(verification_key), ())
                    if str(table_name)
                }
                if not table_names:
                    continue
                self._bootstrap_scope_tables_by_key[verification_key] = table_names
                for table_name in table_names:
                    self._bootstrap_scope_keys_by_table.setdefault(table_name, set()).add(
                        verification_key,
                    )
        elif normalized_existing_tables:
            existing_table_set = set(normalized_existing_tables)
            for verification_key in normalized_verification_keys:
                self._bootstrap_scope_tables_by_key[verification_key] = set(existing_table_set)
            for table_name in existing_table_set:
                self._bootstrap_scope_keys_by_table[table_name] = set(normalized_verification_keys)
        from l2000_connection.connection import BootstrapMode, BootstrapScopeProof

        existing_table_set = set(normalized_existing_tables)
        for verification_key, table_names in self._bootstrap_scope_tables_by_key.items():
            normalized_table_names = tuple(SqlTableName(table_name) for table_name in sorted(table_names))
            exists_by_table = {table_name: table_name in existing_table_set for table_name in normalized_table_names}
            existing_count = sum(1 for exists in exists_by_table.values() if exists)
            mode = (
                BootstrapMode.PRESEEDED
                if normalized_table_names and existing_count == len(normalized_table_names)
                else BootstrapMode.WARM
            )
            self._bootstrap_scope_proof_cache[verification_key] = BootstrapScopeProof(
                mode=mode,
                required_tables=normalized_table_names,
                exists_by_table=BootstrapTableExistenceFacts(tuple(exists_by_table.items())),
                verification_key=BootstrapScopeVerificationKey(verification_key),
                seed_fact_hashes=BootstrapSeedFactHashes(
                    tuple(
                        (BootstrapSeedFactKey(seed_key), BootstrapFactsHash(seed_hash))
                        for seed_key, seed_hash in normalized_seed_fact_hashes.items()
                    ),
                ),
                facts_hash=(
                    BootstrapFactsHash(self._bootstrap_scope_facts_by_key[verification_key])
                    if verification_key in self._bootstrap_scope_facts_by_key
                    else NoBootstrapFactsHash()
                ),
            )
        self._table_exists_cache.clear()
        for table_name in normalized_existing_tables:
            self._record_table_exists_result(SqlTableName(table_name), True)
        self._table_exists_cache_sealed = bool(table_exists_cache_sealed)
        if table_exists_cache_sealed:
            self._table_exists_cache.seal_snapshot()

        self._verified_bootstrap_tables = normalized_bootstrap_tables
        self._verified_domain_bootstrap_tables = normalized_domain_tables
        self._verified_bootstrap_system_session = bool(bootstrap_system_session_verified)

    @pure_lazy
    def resolve_bootstrap_scope_many_lazy(
        self: Self,
        scope_tables_by_key: BootstrapScopeTables,
    ) -> Mapping[str, BootstrapScopeProof]:
        """Return transaction-independent bootstrap facts already owned by this connection."""
        from l2000_connection.connection import BootstrapMode, BootstrapScopeProof

        proofs: dict[str, BootstrapScopeProof] = {}
        unresolved: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
        for verification_key, required_tables in scope_tables_by_key.items():
            key = BootstrapAuthorityKey(verification_key)
            if not key:
                continue
            normalized_tables = tuple(
                dict.fromkeys(SqlTableName(table_name) for table_name in required_tables if str(table_name)),
            )
            if self.is_bootstrap_scope_verified(BootstrapAuthorityKey(key)):
                _record_bootstrap_profile_counter(DiagnosticLabel("bootstrap_proof"), "async_many_verified_hit")
                _record_bootstrap_profile_counter(
                    DiagnosticLabel("bootstrap_proof_tables"), "async_many_verified_hit", len(normalized_tables)
                )
                proofs[key] = BootstrapScopeProof(
                    mode=BootstrapMode.PRESEEDED,
                    required_tables=normalized_tables,
                    exists_by_table=BootstrapTableExistenceFacts(
                        tuple((table_name, True) for table_name in normalized_tables),
                    ),
                    verification_key=BootstrapScopeVerificationKey(key),
                    seed_fact_hashes=BootstrapSeedFactHashes(
                        tuple(
                            (BootstrapSeedFactKey(seed_key), BootstrapFactsHash(seed_hash))
                            for seed_key, seed_hash in self._bootstrap_seed_fact_proof().items()
                        ),
                    ),
                    facts_hash=(
                        self._bootstrap_scope_facts_by_key[key] if key in self._bootstrap_scope_facts_by_key else NoBootstrapFactsHash()
                    ),
                )
                continue

            proof_cache = self._bootstrap_scope_proof_cache
            cached_proof = proof_cache.get(BootstrapAuthorityKey(key))
            if cached_proof is not None and cached_proof.required_tables == normalized_tables:
                _record_bootstrap_profile_counter(DiagnosticLabel("bootstrap_proof"), "async_many_connection_cache_hit")
                _record_bootstrap_profile_counter(
                    DiagnosticLabel("bootstrap_proof_tables"),
                    "async_many_connection_cache_hit",
                    len(normalized_tables),
                )
                proofs[key] = cached_proof
                continue
            unresolved[key] = normalized_tables

        unknown_tables = tuple(
            dict.fromkeys(SqlTableName(table_name) for required_tables in unresolved.values() for table_name in required_tables),
        )
        if unknown_tables:
            from l3200_metadata.bootstrap_state import BootstrapPlanningError

            msg = (
                "resolve_bootstrap_scope_many_lazy() cannot fall back to physical schema probes. "
                "Bootstrap scope facts must be observed through BootstrapInterrogationStep "
                "or supplied by durable/local proof state; there is intentionally no fallback."
            )
            raise BootstrapPlanningError(msg)
        return proofs

    @pure_lazy
    def _resolve_bootstrap_scope_exists_in_schema_transaction_lazy(
        self: Self,
        current_schema_txn: LazySchemaTransaction | None,
        normalized_tables: tuple[SqlTableName, ...],
    ) -> LazyResult[BootstrapScopeExistsMap | None]:
        """Async variant of schema-transaction bootstrap table evidence."""
        return _resolve_bootstrap_scope_exists_in_schema_transaction_impl_lazy(
            current_schema_txn,
            normalized_tables,
        )

    @pure_lazy
    def resolve_bootstrap_scope_for_planning(
        self: Self,
        *,
        required_tables: Sequence[SqlTableName],
        verification_key: BootstrapAuthorityKey | Unset = UNSET,
    ) -> BootstrapScopeProof:
        """Return a cached bootstrap fact without inventing a terminal lazy operation."""
        from l2000_connection.connection import BootstrapMode, BootstrapScopeProof

        normalized_tables = tuple(
            dict.fromkeys(SqlTableName(table_name) for table_name in required_tables if str(table_name)),
        )
        if verification_key is not UNSET:
            proof_cache = self._bootstrap_scope_proof_cache
            cached_proof = proof_cache.get(verification_key)
            if cached_proof is not None and cached_proof.required_tables == normalized_tables:
                _record_bootstrap_profile_counter(DiagnosticLabel("bootstrap_proof"), "async_connection_cache_hit")
                _record_bootstrap_profile_counter(
                    DiagnosticLabel("bootstrap_proof_tables"), "async_connection_cache_hit", len(normalized_tables)
                )
                return cached_proof
        if verification_key is not UNSET:
            _record_bootstrap_profile_counter(DiagnosticLabel("bootstrap_proof"), "async_verified_miss")
            proof_cache = self._bootstrap_scope_proof_cache
            cached_proof = proof_cache.get(verification_key)
            if cached_proof is not None and cached_proof.required_tables == normalized_tables:
                _record_bootstrap_profile_counter(DiagnosticLabel("bootstrap_proof"), "async_connection_cache_hit")
                _record_bootstrap_profile_counter(
                    DiagnosticLabel("bootstrap_proof_tables"), "async_connection_cache_hit", len(normalized_tables)
                )
                return cached_proof
            _record_bootstrap_profile_counter(DiagnosticLabel("bootstrap_proof"), "async_connection_cache_miss")

        if not normalized_tables:
            return BootstrapScopeProof(
                mode=BootstrapMode.WARM,
                required_tables=(),
                exists_by_table=BootstrapTableExistenceFacts(()),
                verification_key=(
                    NO_BOOTSTRAP_SCOPE_VERIFICATION_KEY if verification_key is UNSET else BootstrapScopeVerificationKey(verification_key)
                ),
                seed_fact_hashes=BootstrapSeedFactHashes(
                    tuple(
                        (BootstrapSeedFactKey(seed_key), BootstrapFactsHash(seed_hash))
                        for seed_key, seed_hash in self._bootstrap_seed_fact_proof().items()
                    ),
                ),
            )

        from l3200_metadata.bootstrap_state import BootstrapPlanningError

        msg = (
            "resolve_bootstrap_scope_for_planning() cannot fall back to physical schema probes. "
            "Bootstrap scope facts must be observed through BootstrapInterrogationStep "
            "or supplied by durable/local proof state; there is intentionally no fallback."
        )
        raise BootstrapPlanningError(msg)

    @pure_lazy
    def physical_table_exists_many_lazy(
        self: Self,
        table_names: Sequence[SqlTableName],
    ) -> LazyResult[dict[SqlTableName, bool]]:
        """Async variant of :meth:`physical_table_exists_many`."""
        del table_names
        from l3200_metadata.bootstrap_state import BootstrapPlanningError

        msg = (
            "physical_table_exists_many_lazy() is a forbidden bootstrap probe path. "
            "Use BootstrapInterrogationStep observation rows; there is intentionally no fallback."
        )
        raise BootstrapPlanningError(msg)

    def _mark_table_created(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName) -> None:
        """Mark a table as existing in the cache.

        Backend implementations should call this after successfully creating a table.
        This updates the cache so subsequent ``table_exists()`` calls don't hit the database.

        Args:
            table_name: Name of the table that was created.

        Note:
            If cache is sealed (DDL lockdown enabled), creating a table is a
            correctness error. Lazy bootstrap must explicitly own an unsealed
            schema transition scope before replaying or applying cached DDL.
        """
        if _ConnectionTableCacheMixin.is_table_exists_cache_sealed(self):
            msg = (
                f"Table {table_name!r} marked as created while cache is sealed. "
                "This indicates DDL operations outside the lazy bootstrap schema transition."
            )
            logger.warning(msg)
            return
        self.clear_bootstrap_scope_proof()
        self.invalidate_bootstrap_scope_verification(table_names=(table_name,))
        self._invalidate_column_cache(table_name)
        self._record_table_exists_result(table_name, True)
        known_absent_schema_tables = self._known_absent_schema_tables
        known_absent_schema_tables.discard(table_name)

    def _mark_table_dropped(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName) -> None:
        """Mark a table as absent in the cache after successful DDL."""
        self.clear_bootstrap_scope_proof()
        self.invalidate_bootstrap_scope_verification(table_names=(table_name,))
        self._invalidate_column_cache(table_name)
        self._record_table_exists_result(table_name, False)
        known_absent_schema_tables = self._known_absent_schema_tables
        known_absent_schema_tables.add(table_name)

    @pure_lazy
    def seal_table_exists_cache_lazy(self: Self) -> LazyResult[int]:
        """Seal table-existence cache from connection-local facts only."""
        proven_tables = self.proven_existing_table_snapshot()
        if proven_tables is None:
            raise LazyPurityError(
                "seal_table_exists_cache_lazy() requires authoritative local table facts; "
                "lazy planning cannot list physical tables to seal the cache.",
            )
        return LazyResult.of(
            self._seal_table_exists_cache_from_tables(tuple(proven_tables)),
        )

    @pure_lazy
    def _seal_table_exists_cache_from_tables(
        self: Self,
        all_tables: tuple[SqlTableName, ...],
    ) -> int:
        """Populate and seal the table-exists cache from a known table snapshot."""

        # Clear existing cache to remove stale False entries
        # This ensures the sealed cache accurately reflects current DB state
        self._table_exists_cache.clear()
        self._planning_catalog_snapshot = None
        self._planning_catalog_snapshot_key = None
        self._planning_catalog_model_overlay = None
        self._planning_catalog_model_overlay_base_id = None

        # Pre-populate cache with all existing tables
        for table_name in all_tables:
            self._record_table_exists_result_lazy(table_name, True)

        # Seal the cache - no more DB queries needed
        self._table_exists_cache_sealed = True
        self._table_exists_cache.seal_snapshot()

        return len(all_tables)

    def unseal_table_exists_cache(self: Self) -> None:
        """Unseal the table exists cache when DDL lockdown is disabled.

        This allows ``table_exists()`` to query the database again for
        tables not in the cache. The existing cache entries are preserved
        but new lookups will query the database.

        Note:
            This does NOT clear the cache. Call ``invalidate_table_exists_cache()``
            if you need to clear cached entries.
        """
        self._table_exists_cache_sealed = False
        self._planning_catalog_snapshot = None
        self._planning_catalog_snapshot_key = None
        self._planning_catalog_model_overlay = None
        self._planning_catalog_model_overlay_base_id = None

    def is_table_exists_cache_sealed(self: Self) -> bool:
        """Check if the table exists cache is sealed.

        Returns:
            True if cache is sealed (DDL lockdown enabled), False otherwise.
        """
        if not self._table_exists_cache_sealed:
            return False
        return self._table_exists_cache.has_current_sealed_snapshot()

    @pure_lazy
    def column_exists_lazy(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName, column_name: SqlColumnName) -> LazyResult[bool]:
        """Reject column discovery without projected or snapshot-backed facts."""
        msg = (
            f"column_exists_lazy({table_name}.{column_name}) requires projected schema facts; lazy planning cannot probe physical columns"
        )
        raise LazyPurityError(msg)

    def get_table_indexes(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName) -> Sequence[SqlIndexName]:
        """Get the names of all indexes on a table.

        Args:
            table_name: The name of the table.

        Returns:
            A list of index names.

        Raises:
            db_exc.OperationalError: If an error occurs during the query.
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    def has_index(
        self: Self,
        table_name: SqlTableName,
        columns: Sequence[SqlColumnName],
    ) -> bool:
        """Check if an index exists on the specified columns.

        Uses DDL introspection to check for index existence. This is used by
        pagination methods to detect missing indexes and emit performance warnings.

        Args:
            table_name: Name of the table to check
            columns: Tuple of column names in index order (e.g., ("revision_id", "price"))

        Returns:
            True if an index covering these columns exists, False otherwise

        Note:
            - For versioned tables, check the actual table name (e.g., "products")
            - Column order matters: ("a", "b") is different from ("b", "a")
            - Raises if the table doesn't exist or introspection fails

        Example:
            >>> conn.has_index("products", ("category", "price"))
            True
        """
        del table_name, columns
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "has_index() must be rebuilt on SchemaStateSnapshot index facts; "
            "direct schema introspection was removed by the reconciliation lazy cutover.",
        )

    def create_vector_index(
        self: Self,
        _model_type: type[DatabaseObjectRow[SysId]],
        *,
        dimensions: int | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Create a vector index for a model's vector field.

        This method is called to create a backend-specific vector index.
        Backends with native vector support (PostgreSQL with pgvector, Neo4j)
        should override this to create efficient vector indexes.

        Backends without native vector support use the HNSW polyfill which
        initializes automatically on first use - no index creation needed.

        Args:
            _model_type: The model class with vector field(s)
            dimensions: Optional vector dimensions (some backends require this)

        Example override for PostgreSQL::

            def create_vector_index(self, model_type, *, dimensions=None):
                # Create pgvector HNSW index
                vector_field = get_vector_field(model_type)
                self.execute(CreateIndex(
                    table=model_type.__tablename__,
                    column=vector_field.name,
                    method="hnsw",
                    opclass="vector_cosine_ops"
                ))
        """
        # Default implementation: no-op
        # Backends without native vector indexes use the HNSW polyfill
        # which doesn't require explicit index creation
        _ = dimensions  # Silence unused parameter warning

    def list_indexes(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName) -> Sequence[SqlIndexName]:
        """List all index names on a table.

        Args:
            table_name: Name of table to query

        Returns:
            List of index names (may be unsorted)

        Raises:
            db_exc.OperationalError: If query fails
            ValueError: If table does not exist (backend-specific)
        """
        del table_name
        msg = f"{type(self).__name__} must override list_indexes()"
        raise NotImplementedError(msg)

    def create_index_from_introspection(
        self: Self,
        index_def: IntrospectedIndex,
    ) -> None:
        """Create an index from introspected metadata.

        Generates and executes CREATE INDEX DDL from an IntrospectedIndex structure.

        Args:
            index_def: IntrospectedIndex with index metadata

        Raises:
            db_exc.ProgrammingError: If called inside a transaction
            db_exc.DatabaseError: If index creation fails

        Note:
            - Partial indexes (where_clause) only supported on SQLite/PostgreSQL
            - MariaDB converts partial indexes to full indexes with warning
        """

    async def create_index_from_introspection_async(
        self: Self,
        index_def: IntrospectedIndex,
    ) -> None:
        """Async variant of :meth:`create_index_from_introspection`."""
        del index_def
        msg = f"{type(self).__name__} must override create_index_from_introspection_async()"
        raise NotImplementedError(msg)

    def drop_index(
        self: Self,
        index_name: SqlIndexName,
        table_name: SqlTableName | None = None,
        if_exists: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Drop an index from the database.

        Args:
            index_name: Name of index to drop
            table_name: Table name (required for some backends like SQLite)
            if_exists: If True, don't raise error if index doesn't exist

        Raises:
            db_exc.ProgrammingError: If called inside a transaction
            db_exc.DatabaseError: If drop fails
            ValueError: If index doesn't exist and if_exists=False

        Note:
            - SQLite requires table_name for DROP INDEX
            - Postgres/MariaDB/MongoDB can drop by index name alone
        """

    async def drop_index_async(
        self: Self,
        index_name: SqlIndexName,
        table_name: SqlTableName | None = None,
        if_exists: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        """Async variant of :meth:`drop_index`."""
        del index_name, table_name, if_exists
        msg = f"{type(self).__name__} must override drop_index_async()"
        raise NotImplementedError(msg)

type LazySessionResolve = Callable[[Any], LazyResult[SessionId] | LazyResult[SessionId | None]]
"""Produce the session a plan will act as, from inside that plan.

Takes the plan's read transaction and returns a still-pending
``LazyResult[SessionId]`` or ``LazyResult[SessionId | None]``. A missing value
fails session validation. The parameter is typed loosely because the concrete
transaction class differs between sync and async connections and neither is
nameable here without an import cycle; what a caller is handed is a
``LazyReadTransaction``.

A callback rather than a ``LazyResult`` parameter, and that is forced rather than
chosen. A pending ``LazyResult`` binds to an ``ExecutionContext`` when it is
constructed, so before the plan exists there is no context for the caller to
construct one against, and nothing they could pass. Deferring the call into the
data layer also buys the ordering guarantee: the resolver runs before any caller
step is registered, so there is no window in which a read is registered against
a plan that has no session.
"""


def _register_lazy_session_source(
    scope: SyncPlanScope | AsyncPlanScope,
    resolve: LazySessionResolve | None,
) -> None:
    """Give the plan its session, as a query rather than a value.

    Called immediately after the plan is entered and before the caller has
    registered anything. That is the whole of the ordering guarantee, and the
    reason this is internal rather than something a caller invokes: there is no
    moment at which a caller could do it that is early enough.

    Nothing here executes. ``resolve(txn)`` builds a query and returns its
    ``LazyResult[SessionId]``. The result stays in the plan so generic ServerPlan
    lowering can publish it directly to session initialization without returning
    the identifier to Python.

    The transaction keeps ``SessionId.unresolved()`` in its concrete slot so that
    code reading ``txn.session_id`` sees something inert, and the session
    machinery reads ``_session_id_source`` instead.

    There is no authentication barrier result, and its absence is deliberate. An
    earlier shape registered the resolver's ``LazyResult`` as a plan return so
    that an unresolvable credential would fail the plan rather than read as an
    honest empty result. Inlining makes the barrier redundant: the validation
    statement is itself the barrier, since it looks up whatever the resolver's
    subquery yields and comes back empty when that is NULL, which the reporting
    tier turns into ``SessionValidationError`` -- a 401 at the transport.
    """
    if resolve is None:
        return

    from l2070_batching.server_ref import ScalarServerRef, ServerRefs, inspect_server_value_shape_for_planning

    txn = scope.txn
    plan = txn._get_transaction_plan_lazy()
    existing_step_refs = scope.plan.owned_step_ref_ids()
    lazy_session = resolve(txn)

    # Literal and query resolvers use the same authenticated SQL gate. A literal
    # must not replace the transaction's inert identity or bypass row validation.
    shape = inspect_server_value_shape_for_planning(lazy_session, site="authenticated_session_lazy")
    principal_source: LazyResult[SessionId] | LazyResult[SessionId | None]
    principal_ref: ScalarServerRef[SessionId]
    if shape.has_literal_value:
        settled = shape.literal_value
        if settled is None:
            raise SessionValidationError(
                "The credential presented does not identify a session; a login is required.",
                reason="not_found",
            )
        concrete = settled if isinstance(settled, SessionId) else SessionId(str(settled))
        from impl.common.l2070_server_plan.steps.return_value import SqlScalarLiteralStep
        from l2055_lazy_result.lazy_result import LazyResult

        source = LazyResult.of(concrete)
        source_ref = plan._next_ref()
        plan.semantic_plan_builder.add_step(SqlScalarLiteralStep(source_ref, concrete))
        principal_source = source
        principal_ref = ServerRefs.from_step(plan, source_ref, variant="scalar", type_hint=SessionId)
    else:
        resolver_ref_id = shape.symbolic_ref_id
        new_steps = [step for step in plan._steps if step.ref_id not in existing_step_refs]
        registered_ref = str(new_steps[0].ref_id) if len(new_steps) == 1 else None
        projected_ref = None if resolver_ref_id is None else str(resolver_ref_id)
        if registered_ref is None or (
            projected_ref != registered_ref and (projected_ref is None or not projected_ref.startswith(f"{registered_ref}."))
        ):
            registered = ", ".join(str(step.ref_id) for step in new_steps) or "none"
            raise db_exc.ProgrammingError(
                "An authenticated session resolver must add exactly one query that publishes "
                f"one scalar SessionId; observed plan steps: {registered}.",
            )
        if resolver_ref_id is None:
            raise db_exc.ProgrammingError(
                "An authenticated session resolver must publish one scalar SessionId reference.",
            )
        principal_source = lazy_session
        principal_ref = ServerRefs.from_ref_id(resolver_ref_id, variant="scalar", type_hint=SessionId)

    from impl.common.l2070_server_plan.steps.intent_session import ValidateSessionIntent

    validation_ref = plan._next_ref()
    txn._register_authenticated_principal(principal_source, principal_ref, validation_ref)
    plan.semantic_plan_builder.add_step(ValidateSessionIntent(validation_ref, SessionId.unresolved()))
    plan.semantic_plan_builder.register_authenticated_session_validation_ref(validation_ref)

def _resolve_bootstrap_scope_exists_from_schema_facts(
    current_schema_txn: SchemaBootstrapEvidence,
    normalized_tables: tuple[SqlTableName, ...],
) -> BootstrapScopeExistsMap:
    """Materialize bootstrap existence from already-authorized schema facts."""
    from l3200_metadata.bootstrap_state import BootstrapPlanningError

    if not isinstance(current_schema_txn, SchemaBootstrapEvidence):
        msg = "schema-transaction bootstrap evidence requires active schema planning state"
        raise BootstrapPlanningError(msg)

    results = BootstrapScopeExistsMap()
    unknown_tables: list[SqlTableName] = []
    for table_name in normalized_tables:
        known = current_schema_txn.projected_or_cached_table_exists(table_name)
        if isinstance(known, bool):
            results[SqlTableName(table_name)] = known
        else:
            unknown_tables.append(table_name)
    if unknown_tables:
        batch_results = current_schema_txn.table_exists_many_for_schema_batch(tuple(unknown_tables))
        for table_name in unknown_tables:
            results[SqlTableName(table_name)] = bool(batch_results.get(table_name, False))
    return results

class _ConnectionStateAndCompositionBase(  # pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleMethodOverride, reportIncompatibleVariableOverride]
    ConnectionPayloadOpaqueMarker,
    _LazyConnectionBase,
    _ConnectionSqlCompatibilityMixin,
    _ConnectionTransactionExecutionMixin,
    _ConnectionCallbackExecutionMixin,
    _ConnectionSchemaIntrospectionMixin,
    _ConnectionCoreSupportMixin,
    BackendTypeOwner,
):
    """State and shared composition base for active database connections.

    Methods may raise exceptions from ``data_layer.exceptions``
    (e.g., ``db_exc.OperationalError``, ``db_exc.IntegrityError``) upon failure.

    Lifecycle contract:
        Connection usage is explicit: create, connect, use transaction entrypoints,
        then close. Transaction methods are valid only while connected.

    State semantics:
        Data transactions (read/write/versioned) and schema transactions are
        mutually exclusive and non-nestable.

    Mode contract:
        Public callers use ``SyncDatabaseConnection`` or
        ``AsyncDatabaseConnection`` facades. Those facades expose only their own
        mode's lifecycle, schema, session, and version handles. Backend
        implementations share this core for common state and private helper
        logic.

    Thread Safety:
        Database connections are not thread-safe and must not be shared across threads.
        The connection tracks which thread created it and will raise ProgrammingError
        if accessed from a different thread.
    """

    _startup_schema_observation_mode: StartupSchemaObservationMode = StartupSchemaObservationMode.STANDARD

    def configure_startup_schema_observation(
        self: Self,
        mode: StartupSchemaObservationMode,
    ) -> None:
        """Select the initial schema-observation path before driver open."""
        self._startup_schema_observation_mode = mode

    def _table_exists_uncached_under_authority(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName) -> bool:
        """Probe one physical table name under the schema/capability authority boundary."""
        with _imp_impl_l2070_execution_context().server_plan_execution_context():
            return self._table_exists_uncached(table_name)

    async def _table_exists_uncached_under_authority_async(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName) -> bool:
        """Async single-table physical existence probe under schema/capability authority."""
        with _imp_impl_l2070_execution_context().server_plan_execution_context():
            return await self._table_exists_uncached_async(table_name)

    def _validated_cached_table_exists(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName) -> CachedTableExistsProof:
        """Return a validated cached table-existence result, if present."""
        self._validate_table_exists_args(table_name)
        cached = self._table_exists_from_cache(table_name)
        return CachedTableExistsProof(found=True, exists=bool(cached)) if cached is not None else CachedTableExistsProof(found=False)

    def _record_authoritative_table_exists(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName, exists: bool) -> bool:
        """Record one authoritative table-existence result and return it."""
        self._record_table_exists_result(SqlTableName(table_name), exists)
        return exists

    def table_exists(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName) -> bool:
        """Check if a table exists in the database (cached).

        Results are cached per connection. The cache is updated when tables
        are created via ``create_table_from_schema()``. When DDL lockdown is
        enabled, the cache is sealed and no database queries are needed.

        Args:
            table_name: The name of the table to check.

        Returns:
            True if the table exists, False otherwise.

        Raises:
            db_exc.OperationalError: If an error occurs during the check.
        """
        cached = self._validated_cached_table_exists(table_name)
        if cached.found:
            return cached.exists
        return self._record_authoritative_table_exists(
            table_name,
            self._table_exists_uncached_under_authority(table_name),
        )

    async def table_exists_async(self: Self, table_name: SqlTableName) -> bool:
        """Check if a table exists in the database (cached), async variant.

        Async variant of :meth:`table_exists`. Uses the same in-memory cache
        and calls :meth:`_table_exists_uncached_async` on cache miss.

        Args:
            table_name: The name of the table to check.

        Returns:
            True if the table exists, False otherwise.

        Raises:
            db_exc.OperationalError: If an error occurs during the check.
        """
        cached = self._validated_cached_table_exists(table_name)
        if cached.found:
            return cached.exists
        return self._record_authoritative_table_exists(
            table_name,
            await self._table_exists_uncached_under_authority_async(table_name),
        )

    def table_exists_many(self: Self, table_names: Sequence[SqlTableName]) -> TableExistsManyResult:
        """Check many table names with one schema listing on cache misses."""
        cached_partition = _cached_table_existence(self, table_names)
        result = cached_partition.known
        for table_name in cached_partition.missing:
            exists = self._table_exists_uncached_under_authority(table_name)
            self._record_table_exists_result(SqlTableName(table_name), exists)
            result[table_name] = exists
        return TableExistsManyResult(result)

    async def table_exists_many_async(self: Self, table_names: Sequence[SqlTableName]) -> TableExistsManyResult:
        """Check many table names with one schema listing on cache misses."""
        cached_partition = _cached_table_existence(self, table_names)
        result = cached_partition.known
        for table_name in cached_partition.missing:
            exists = await self._table_exists_uncached_under_authority_async(table_name)
            self._record_table_exists_result(SqlTableName(table_name), exists)
            result[table_name] = exists
        return TableExistsManyResult(result)

    def resolve_bootstrap_scope_many(
        self: Self,
        scope_tables_by_key: BootstrapScopeTablesByKey,
    ) -> BootstrapScopeProofMap:
        """Resolve many named bootstrap proof scopes through the memoized provider."""
        proofs = BootstrapScopeProofMap()
        unresolved: BootstrapScopeTablesByKey = BootstrapScopeTablesByKey()
        for verification_key, required_tables in scope_tables_by_key.items():
            key = BootstrapScopeKey(str(verification_key))
            if not key:
                continue
            normalized_tables = tuple(dict.fromkeys(SqlTableName(table_name) for table_name in required_tables if str(table_name)))
            authority_key = BootstrapAuthorityKey(key)
            if self.is_bootstrap_scope_verified(authority_key):
                _record_bootstrap_profile_counter(DiagnosticLabel("bootstrap_proof"), "many_verified_hit")

        that subsequent ``table_exists()`` calls never hit the database.

def _summarize_detailed_transaction_timing() -> str | None:  # broad-type: accepted
    payload = get_detailed_timing_payload()
    if not payload:
        return optional_branded_text(None, str)

    parts: list[str] = []
    for section_name in ("write_transaction", "versioned_write", "system_session_bootstrap"):
        section = payload.get(section_name)
        if isinstance(section, dict):
            timings = ", ".join(
                f"{key}={value}" for key, value in section.items() if key.endswith("_ms") and isinstance(value, int | float)
            )
            if timings:
                parts.append(f"{section_name}({timings})")

    pipelines = payload.get("pipelines")
    if isinstance(pipelines, list) and pipelines:
        aggregate_keys = ("prepare_ms", "lower_ms", "optimize_ms", "compile_ms", "execute_ms")
        aggregate_values: dict[str, float] = dict.fromkeys(aggregate_keys, 0.0)
        for pipeline in pipelines:
            if not isinstance(pipeline, dict):
                continue
            for key in aggregate_keys:
                value = pipeline.get(key)
                if isinstance(value, int | float):
                    aggregate_values[key] += float(value)
        parts.append(
            "pipelines_total("
            f"count={len(pipelines)}, " + ", ".join(f"{key}={round(value, 3)}" for key, value in aggregate_values.items()) + ")",
        )
        pipeline_parts: list[str] = []
        for pipeline in pipelines[:3]:
            if not isinstance(pipeline, dict):
                continue
            pipeline_parts.append(
                "pipeline("
                f"prepare_ms={pipeline.get('prepare_ms')}, "
                f"lower_ms={pipeline.get('lower_ms')}, "
                f"optimize_ms={pipeline.get('optimize_ms')}, "
                f"compile_ms={pipeline.get('compile_ms')}, "
                f"execute_ms={pipeline.get('execute_ms')}, "
                f"steps={pipeline.get('backend_step_count')}, "
                f"groups={pipeline.get('backend_execution_group_count')}, "
                f"workflow_boundary={pipeline.get('workflow_boundary')}, "
                f"summary={pipeline.get('step_summary')}"
                ")",
            )
        if len(pipelines) > 3:
            pipeline_parts.append(f"+{len(pipelines) - 3} more pipelines")
        parts.extend(pipeline_parts)

    return optional_branded_text("; ".join(parts) if parts else None, str)

    This is returned by :meth:`_DatabaseConnectionCore.health` and provides information
    about the current state of the database connection and backend.

    Attributes
    ----------

    status : HealthStatus
        Overall health status (healthy, degraded, unhealthy)

    Example
    -------

        result = conn.health()
        if result.status == HealthStatus.HEALTHY:
            print("Database is healthy")
        else:
            print(f"Database issue: {result.message}")

    Notes
    -----

    This check is designed to be fast and non-intrusive. It does not
    include sensitive information (credentials, connection strings) or
    perform expensive operations (full table scans, complex queries).

    See Also
    --------

    :class:`HealthStatus` : The health status enumeration
    :meth:`_DatabaseConnectionCore.health` : The health check method
    """

        return {

            HealthCheckResultKey.BACKEND: self.backend,

            HealthCheckResultKey.MESSAGE: self.message,
            HealthCheckResultKey.DETAILS: copy.deepcopy(self.details),

class DatabaseRow:
    """Wrapper class for database rows from different backends.

    Provides a uniform interface to access row data regardless of the backend.

    Access Methods:
        - By index: row[0], row[1] (positional access)
        - By name: row["column_name"] (named access)
        - Iterate: for value in row (iterate over values)
        - Keys: row.keys() (get column names)
        - Length: len(row) (get number of columns)

    Conversion:
        - To dict: dict(zip(row.keys(), row))
        - To list: list(row)

    Note:
        DatabaseRow implements the Sequence protocol, so it can be used
        anywhere a sequence is expected.
    """

    row: SupportsRowInterface  #: The backend-specific row object (sqlite3.Row, psycopg.Row, etc.)

    _translator: Callable[[Exception], Exception]  #: Function to translate backend exceptions (private implementation detail)

    def __init__(
        self: DatabaseRow,
        row: SupportsRowInterface,
        translator: Callable[[Exception], Exception],
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize a DatabaseRow.

        Args:
            row: The backend-specific row object.
            translator: Function to translate backend exceptions to our exception types.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If row is None or falsy.
        """
        if not row:
            msg = "Row cannot be None"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        self.row = row
        self._translator = translator

    def __getitem__(self: DatabaseRow, key: int | str) -> Any:
        """Get a column value by index or name."""
        try:
            return self.row.__getitem__(key)
        except Exception as e:
            raise self._translator(e) from e

    def __len__(self: DatabaseRow) -> int:
        """Get the number of columns."""
        try:
            return self.row.__len__()
        except Exception as e:
            raise self._translator(e) from e

    def __iter__(self: DatabaseRow) -> Iterator[Any]:
        """Iterate over column values.

        Handles dict-like rows (psycopg3 dict_row) by iterating over values,
        not keys. For sequence-like rows (sqlite3.Row, tuples), iterates normally.
        """
        try:
            # Key-aware rows may iterate keys by default; publish values so
            # ``dict(zip(row.keys(), row))`` stays backend-independent.
            keys = self.row.keys
            if callable(keys):
                return iter(self.row[key] for key in keys())
            return self.row.__iter__()
        except Exception as e:
            raise self._translator(e) from e

    def __repr__(self: DatabaseRow) -> DiagnosticMessage:
        """String representation of the row."""
        try:
            return DiagnosticMessage(f"DatabaseRow({self.row})")
        except Exception as e:
            raise self._translator(e) from e

    def keys(self: DatabaseRow) -> tuple[DatabaseColumnLabel, ...]:
        """Get the column names.

        Returns:
            List of column names in the row
        """
        try:
            return tuple(DatabaseColumnLabel(str(key)) for key in self.row.keys())
        except Exception as e:
            raise self._translator(e) from e

    def items(self: DatabaseRow) -> tuple[tuple[DatabaseColumnLabel, Any], ...]:
        """Return column/value pairs for mapping-style row consumers."""
        try:
            return tuple(
                (DatabaseColumnLabel(str(key)), self.row.__getitem__(key))
                for key in self.row.keys()
            )
        except Exception as e:
            raise self._translator(e) from e

    def __contains__(self: DatabaseRow, key: object) -> bool:
        """Check if a column name exists in the row.

        Args:
            key: Column name to check

        Returns:
            True if column exists, False otherwise
        """
        try:
            if hasattr(self.row, "__contains__"):
                return bool(self.row.__contains__(key))  # pyright: ignore[reportAttributeAccessIssue]
            # Fallback for backends without __contains__
            return isinstance(key, str) and key in self.row.keys()
        except Exception as e:
            raise self._translator(e) from e

"""Async executor protocol for native async database I/O.

This module defines the protocol that all database backends must implement
to provide native async database operations. This is the foundation of the
async-first architecture where:

1. Async methods use native async I/O.
2. Sync methods use their own sync backend adapters and must not run event loops.

By implementing this protocol, backends can use their native async drivers:
- SQLite: aiosqlite
- PostgreSQL: psycopg AsyncConnection
- MariaDB/DoltDB: aiomysql
- MongoDB: Motor
- Neo4j: AsyncDriver

Architecture Note
-----------------

The async-first architecture flips the traditional pattern:

**OLD (sync-first):**
    def execute(sql, params):  # Actual implementation
        return _do_database_work()

    async def execute_async(sql, params):  # Wrapper
        return await _thread_pool_wrapper(self.execute, sql, params)

**NEW (mode-separated):**
    async def execute_async(sql, params):  # Actual implementation
        return await _async_driver.execute(sql, params)

    def execute(sql, params):  # Sync implementation
        return _sync_driver.execute(sql, params)

This eliminates thread-pool overhead for async callers without making sync callers
drive an event loop.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, NewType

from l1400_types import SqlParamTuple
from collections.abc import Sequence

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from l2000_connection.connection_models import DatabaseRow

AsyncSqlText = NewType("AsyncSqlText", str)


class NoSqlParams:
    pass


class NoDatabaseRow:
    pass


_NO_SQL_PARAMS = NoSqlParams()

type AsyncSqlParams = SqlParamTuple | NoSqlParams
type AsyncDatabaseRowResult = DatabaseRow | NoDatabaseRow


class AsyncExecutor(ABC):
    """Protocol for native async database execution.

    All SQL-based backends must implement this protocol to provide
    truly async database I/O without thread pool overhead.

    The methods in this protocol are the async implementation.
    Sync equivalents must use sync backend adapters rather than running an event loop.

    Implementation Notes
    --------------------

    Each backend should implement these methods using their native async driver:

    * SQLite: ``aiosqlite`` (note: pseudo-async via internal threads)
    * PostgreSQL: ``psycopg.AsyncConnection``
    * MariaDB/DoltDB: ``aiomysql``
    * MongoDB: ``motor.motor_asyncio.AsyncIOMotorClient``
    * Neo4j: ``neo4j.AsyncDriver``

    The connection object should maintain an internal async cursor/state
    so that execute_async() followed by fetchone_async()/fetchall_async()
    works correctly without requiring the cursor to be passed explicitly.
    """

    # Internal state that backends must maintain
    # _async_cursor: The cursor from the last execute_async() call

    @abstractmethod
    async def execute_async(
        self: AsyncExecutor,
        sql: AsyncSqlText,
        params: AsyncSqlParams = _NO_SQL_PARAMS,
    ) -> None:
        """Execute SQL statement asynchronously.

        This is the async-native execution method. Sync execution is owned by
        separate sync backend adapters.

        After execution, the internal cursor is stored for subsequent
        fetchone_async()/fetchall_async() calls.

        Args:
            sql: SQL statement to execute
            params: Query parameters

        Raises:
            DatabaseError: On execution failure
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    async def execute_many_async(
        self: AsyncExecutor,
        sql: AsyncSqlText,
        params_list: Sequence[SqlParamTuple],
    ) -> int:
        """Execute SQL statement with multiple parameter sets asynchronously.

        Args:
            sql: SQL statement to execute
            params_list: List of parameter tuples

        Returns:
            Number of rows affected

        Raises:
            DatabaseError: On execution failure
        """
        params_list = tuple(params_list)
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    async def fetchone_async(self: AsyncExecutor) -> AsyncDatabaseRowResult:
        """Fetch one row from the last query asynchronously.

        Uses the internal cursor from the previous execute_async() call.

        Returns:
            Row as dictionary, or None if no more rows
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    async def fetchall_async(self: AsyncExecutor) -> tuple[DatabaseRow, ...]:
        """Fetch all rows from the last query asynchronously.

        Uses the internal cursor from the previous execute_async() call.

        Returns:
            Tuple of rows as dictionaries
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    async def fetchmany_async(
        self: AsyncExecutor,
        size: int,
    ) -> tuple[DatabaseRow, ...]:
        """Fetch up to ``size`` rows from the last query asynchronously.

        Uses the internal cursor from the previous execute_async() call.

        Args:
            size: Maximum number of rows to fetch

        Returns:
            Tuple of rows as dictionaries
        """
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    async def commit_async(self: AsyncExecutor) -> None:
        """Commit the current transaction asynchronously."""
        raise NotImplementedError

    @abstractmethod
    async def rollback_async(self: AsyncExecutor) -> None:
        """Rollback the current transaction asynchronously."""
        raise NotImplementedError
