                                probe_outcome.__traceback__,
                            ),
                        )
                        await self._evict_connection_async(
                            candidate_p,
                            "liveness check error during sweep",
                        )
                        continue
                    alive = probe_outcome

                    if alive:
                        with self._lock:
                            candidate_p.in_use = False
                    else:
                        await self._evict_connection_async(
                            candidate_p,
                            "dead during health sweep",
                        )

                # Evict idle connections that have exceeded max_idle_time.
                # This runs AFTER health sweep so dead connections are already
                # removed and don't inflate the count toward min_size.
                now = time.monotonic()
                idle_evictions: list[_PooledConnection[ConnT]] = []
                with self._lock:
                    for p in self._connections:
                        if (
                            not p.in_use
                            and (now - p.last_used_at) > self._config.max_idle_time
                            and (len(self._connections) - len(idle_evictions)) > self._config.min_size
                        ):
                            idle_evictions.append(p)
                    for idle in idle_evictions:
                        if idle in self._connections:
                            self._connections.remove(idle)
                            self._idle_connections_evicted += 1
                        else:
                            self._eviction_races += 1
                            logger.warning(
                                "Idle connection already removed during eviction (race_count=%d)",
                                self._eviction_races,
                            )

                for idle in idle_evictions:
                    logger.info(
                        "Idle connection evicted (idle_time=%.0fs, max_idle=%.0fs, pool_size=%d)",
                        now - idle.last_used_at,
                        self._config.max_idle_time,
                        self.size,
                    )
                    try:
                        idle.connection.close()
                    except Exception as e:
                        logger.debug("Error closing idle connection: %s", e)

            except asyncio.CancelledError:
                logger.debug("Pool maintenance task cancelled")
                raise
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning("Error in pool maintenance: %s", e)

        logger.debug("Pool maintenance stopped")

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def _acquire_async(self) -> AsyncGenerator[ConnT]:
        """Acquire a connection from the pool.

        This method NEVER blocks waiting for a connection. If all pooled
        connections are in use, it creates an ephemeral connection to
        avoid deadlocks in re-entrant scenarios.

        The connection is automatically released when the context manager
        exits, even if an exception is raised.

        Yields
        ------
        ConnT
            A database connection ready for use

        Example
        -------
        ::

            async with pool.acquire() as conn:
                session = conn.session(session_id)
                result = session.read(lambda txn: txn.query(Model).execute())
        """
        if not self._initialized:
            await self._initialize_async()

        pooled: _PooledConnection[ConnT] | None = None
        ephemeral: ConnT | None = None
        acquire_start = time.monotonic()  # Track when connection was acquired for active time

        # Track pool checkout time
        timing_enabled = _imp_api_l2092_timing_tracking().is_timing_tracking_enabled()
        checkout_start = time.monotonic() if timing_enabled else None

        try:
            # Validate-on-checkout: take one candidate at a time under the lock,
            # check liveness OUTSIDE the lock (is_connected() may do I/O), and
            # loop until we find a live connection or exhaust candidates.
            dead_connections: list[_PooledConnection[ConnT]] = []
            need_new_pooled = False

            while pooled is None:
                candidate: _PooledConnection[ConnT] | None = None
                with self._lock:
                    for p in self._connections:
                        if not p.in_use:
                            p.in_use = True  # Reserve it
                            candidate = p
                            break
                    if candidate is None:
                        # No idle candidates left
                        need_new_pooled = len(self._connections) < self._config.max_size
                        break

                # Check liveness OUTSIDE the lock.  Skip the check entirely
                # if the connection was returned to the pool recently (within
                # the grace period), since it is almost certainly still alive.
                # When a check IS needed, use the async variant so the event
                # loop is not blocked by sync I/O in is_connected().
                # If CancelledError fires during the await, release the
                # reserved candidate so it doesn't leak as permanently in_use.
                try:
                    alive = self._should_skip_liveness_check(candidate) or await self._is_connection_alive_async(
                        candidate.connection,
                    )
                except asyncio.CancelledError:
                    # Evict (don't just release) because the async liveness
                    # operation may still be in flight. Releasing would allow
                    # acquire() to hand the connection to user code while the
                    # driver is still accessing it.
                    await self._evict_connection_async(candidate, "liveness check cancelled")
                    # Close dead connections accumulated before cancellation
                    # so their handles are not leaked.
                    await self._close_dead_connections_async(
                        tuple(dead_connections),
                        during="checkout cancellation",
                    )
                    raise
                except db_exc.ProgrammingError:
                    if (
                        candidate.connection.backend_type != BackendType.POSTGRES
                        or candidate.connection.should_use_native_async_liveness_probe()
                    ):
                        with self._lock:
                            if candidate in self._connections:
                                candidate.in_use = False
                        await self._close_dead_connections_async(
                            tuple(dead_connections),
                            during="checkout ProgrammingError",
                        )
                        raise
                    dead_connections.append(candidate)
                    with self._lock:
                        if candidate in self._connections:
                            self._connections.remove(candidate)
                            self._dead_connections_evicted += 1
                    await self._close_dead_connections_async(
                        tuple(dead_connections),
                        during="checkout ProgrammingError",
                    )
                    dead_connections.clear()
                    continue
                except Exception:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Liveness check raised during checkout",
                        exc_info=True,
                    )
                    dead_connections.append(candidate)
                    with self._lock:
                        if candidate in self._connections:
                            self._connections.remove(candidate)
                            self._dead_connections_evicted += 1
                    await self._close_dead_connections_async(
                        tuple(dead_connections),
                        during="checkout liveness exception",
                    )
                    dead_connections.clear()
                    raise
                if alive:
                    pooled = candidate
                    with self._lock:
                        pooled.last_used_at = time.monotonic()
                        pooled.acquired_at = time.monotonic()
                else:
                    # Dead -- evict under lock, close outside
                    dead_connections.append(candidate)
                    with self._lock:
                        if candidate in self._connections:
                            self._connections.remove(candidate)
                            self._dead_connections_evicted += 1
                        else:
                            self._eviction_races += 1
                            logger.warning(
                                "Dead connection already removed during checkout (race_count=%d)",
                                self._eviction_races,
                            )
                    await self._close_dead_connections_async(
                        tuple(dead_connections),
                        during="checkout liveness error",
                    )
                    dead_connections.clear()

            # Close dead connections outside the lock (close() may block)
            await self._close_dead_connections_async(tuple(dead_connections), during="checkout")

            # Create connection outside the lock to avoid blocking other acquires
            if need_new_pooled:
                conn = await self._create_connection()
                with self._lock:
                    # Re-check in case another coroutine created one
                    if len(self._connections) < self._config.max_size:
                        pooled = _PooledConnection(
                            connection=conn,
                            in_use=True,
                            acquired_at=time.monotonic(),
                        )
                        self._connections.append(pooled)
                    else:
                        # Pool filled while we were creating - use as ephemeral
                        ephemeral = conn
                        self._ephemeral_count += 1

            if pooled is not None:
                with self._lock:
                    self._total_acquisitions += 1
                # Record pool checkout time (fast path - found existing connection)
                if checkout_start is not None:
                    checkout_time_ms = (time.monotonic() - checkout_start) * 1000.0
                    _imp_api_l2092_timing_tracking().record_pool_checkout_timing(checkout_time_ms)
                # Got a pooled connection
                elapsed_ms = (time.monotonic() - acquire_start) * 1000.0
                logger.info(
                    "Connection taken from pool pool_size=%d available=%d elapsed_ms=%.2f",
                    self.size,
                    self.available,
                    elapsed_ms,
                )
                yield pooled.connection
            elif ephemeral is not None:
                with self._lock:
                    self._total_acquisitions += 1
                # Record pool checkout time (created new connection, but pool filled while creating)
                if checkout_start is not None:
                    checkout_time_ms = (time.monotonic() - checkout_start) * 1000.0
                    _imp_api_l2092_timing_tracking().record_pool_checkout_timing(checkout_time_ms)
                # Ephemeral was set because pool filled while we were creating
                elapsed_ms = (time.monotonic() - acquire_start) * 1000.0
                logger.info(
                    "Connection taken (ephemeral, pool filled during creation) pool_size=%d elapsed_ms=%.2f",
                    self.size,
                    elapsed_ms,
                )
                yield ephemeral
            else:
                # All pooled connections in use and at max_size
                # Create ephemeral connection to avoid blocking/deadlock
                logger.debug(
                    "Pool exhausted (size=%d, max=%d), creating ephemeral connection",
                    self.size,
                    self._config.max_size,
                )
                ephemeral = await self._create_connection()
                # Increment counters AFTER successful creation, inside lock for thread safety
                with self._lock:
                    self._ephemeral_count += 1
                    self._total_acquisitions += 1
                # Record pool checkout time AFTER ephemeral connection creation
                if checkout_start is not None:
                    checkout_time_ms = (time.monotonic() - checkout_start) * 1000.0
                    _imp_api_l2092_timing_tracking().record_pool_checkout_timing(checkout_time_ms)
                elapsed_ms = (time.monotonic() - acquire_start) * 1000.0
                logger.info(
                    "Connection taken (ephemeral, pool exhausted) pool_size=%d max_size=%d elapsed_ms=%.2f",
                    self.size,
                    self._config.max_size,
                    elapsed_ms,
                )
                yield ephemeral

        finally:
            active_time_ms = (time.monotonic() - acquire_start) * 1000.0
            if pooled is not None:
                # Check if connection is still alive before returning to pool.
                # If it died during use (e.g., server killed it), evict instead
                # of returning a dead connection that will fail for the next caller.
                # Use async liveness check to avoid blocking the event loop.
                # If CancelledError fires here, evict and re-raise so the
                # connection doesn't leak as permanently in_use.
                try:
                    alive = await self._is_connection_alive_async(
                        pooled.connection,
                    )
                except asyncio.CancelledError:
                    await self._evict_connection_async(pooled, "liveness check cancelled")
                    logger.info(
                        "Connection evicted after liveness check cancellation active_time_ms=%.2f",
                        active_time_ms,
                    )
                    raise
                except db_exc.ProgrammingError:
                    await self._evict_connection_async(
                        pooled,
                        "liveness ProgrammingError after use",
                    )
                    raise
                except Exception:
                    logger.warning(
                        "Liveness check raised during return to pool",
                        exc_info=True,
                    )
                    await self._evict_connection_async(pooled, "liveness check error after use")
                    raise
                if not alive:
                    await self._evict_connection_async(pooled, "dead after use")
                    logger.info(
                        "Dead connection evicted after use active_time_ms=%.2f",
                        active_time_ms,
                    )
                else:
                    # Clean up connection state before returning to pool.
                    # If cleanup fails, the connection is likely in an error state
                    # (e.g., PostgreSQL "current transaction is aborted") and must
                    # be evicted rather than returned to the pool.
                    # CancelledError is handled separately: we evict the connection
                    # AND re-raise to honour Python's cancellation protocol.
                    try:
                        await self._cleanup_connection_state(pooled.connection)
                    except asyncio.CancelledError:
                        await self._evict_connection_async(pooled, "cleanup cancelled")
                        logger.info(
                            "Connection evicted after cleanup cancellation active_time_ms=%.2f",
                            active_time_ms,
                        )
                        raise
                    except Exception:
                        self._cleanup_failures += 1
                        logger.warning(
                            "Connection cleanup failed on return to pool (cleanup_failures=%d)",
                            self._cleanup_failures,
                            exc_info=True,
                        )
                        await self._evict_connection_async(pooled, "cleanup failed on return")
                        logger.info(
                            "Connection evicted after cleanup failure active_time_ms=%.2f",
                            active_time_ms,
                        )
                        raise
                    else:
                        # Return pooled connection to pool
                        with self._lock:
                            pooled.in_use = False
                            pooled.last_used_at = time.monotonic()
                            pooled.acquired_at = None
                        logger.info(
                            "Connection returned to pool pool_size=%d available=%d active_time_ms=%.2f",
                            self.size,
                            self.available,
                            active_time_ms,
                        )
            elif ephemeral is not None:
                # Close ephemeral connection
                try:
                    await ephemeral.close_async()
                    logger.info(
                        "Connection closed (ephemeral) active_time_ms=%.2f",
                        active_time_ms,
                    )
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.warning("Error closing ephemeral connection: %s", e)

    # =========================================================================
    # Synchronous Acquisition Methods
    # =========================================================================

    def _acquire_sync(self) -> ConnT:
        """Synchronously acquire a connection from the pool.

        This method is designed for sync code running through an application-owned
        thread-pool adapter in async applications. It NEVER blocks
        waiting for a connection - if all pooled connections are in use,
        it creates an ephemeral connection.

        You MUST call ``release_sync()`` when done with the connection,
        or use ``acquire_sync_context()`` which handles release automatically.

        Returns
        -------
        ConnT
            A database connection ready for use

        Raises
        ------
        RuntimeError
            If pool is not initialized (call ``initialize()`` first)

        Example
        -------
        ::

            # In async code using an application-owned thread pool
            async def run_query():
                def sync_work():
                    conn = pool.acquire_sync()
                    try:
                        session = conn.session(SessionId.system())
                        return session.read(lambda txn: txn.query(Model).execute())
                    finally:
                        pool.release_sync(conn)
                return await run_sync_in_worker(sync_work)
        """
        if not self._initialized:
            self._initialize_sync()

        pooled: _PooledConnection[ConnT] | None = None
        ephemeral: ConnT | None = None
        acquire_start = time.monotonic()  # Track when connection was acquired for active time

        # Track pool checkout time (same as async acquire)
        timing_enabled = _imp_api_l2092_timing_tracking().is_timing_tracking_enabled()
        checkout_start = time.monotonic() if timing_enabled else None

        # Validate-on-checkout: take one candidate at a time under the lock,
        # check liveness OUTSIDE the lock (is_connected() may do I/O).
        # Skip the check for connections used recently (within grace period).
        dead_connections: list[_PooledConnection[ConnT]] = []
        need_new_pooled = False

        while pooled is None:
            candidate: _PooledConnection[ConnT] | None = None
            with self._lock:
                for p in self._connections:
                    if not p.in_use:
                        p.in_use = True  # Reserve it
                        candidate = p
                        break
                if candidate is None:
                    need_new_pooled = len(self._connections) < self._config.max_size
                    break

            # Check liveness OUTSIDE the lock (may do I/O).
            # Skip the check if the connection was used recently.
            try:
                alive = self._should_skip_liveness_check(candidate) or self._is_connection_alive(candidate.connection)
            except db_exc.ProgrammingError:
                with self._lock:
                    if candidate in self._connections:
                        candidate.in_use = False
                self._close_dead_connections(
                    tuple(dead_connections),
                    during="sync checkout ProgrammingError",
                )
                raise
            except Exception:
                logger.warning(
                    "Liveness check raised during sync checkout",
                    exc_info=True,
                )
                dead_connections.append(candidate)
                with self._lock:
                    if candidate in self._connections:
                        self._connections.remove(candidate)
                        self._dead_connections_evicted += 1
                    else:
                        self._eviction_races += 1
                        logger.warning(
                            "Dead connection already removed during sync checkout (race_count=%d)",
                            self._eviction_races,
                        )
                self._close_dead_connections(
                    tuple(dead_connections),
                    during="sync checkout liveness error",
                )
                raise
            if alive:
                pooled = candidate
                with self._lock:
                    pooled.last_used_at = time.monotonic()
                    pooled.acquired_at = time.monotonic()
            else:
                dead_connections.append(candidate)
                with self._lock:
                    if candidate in self._connections:
                        self._connections.remove(candidate)
                        self._dead_connections_evicted += 1
                    else:
                        self._eviction_races += 1
                        logger.warning(
                            "Dead connection already removed during sync checkout (race_count=%d)",
                            self._eviction_races,
                        )

        # Close dead connections outside the lock
        self._close_dead_connections(tuple(dead_connections), during="sync checkout")

        # Create connection outside the lock to avoid blocking other acquires
        # Uses DNS resolution and timeout, same as async path
        if need_new_pooled:
            conn = self._create_connection_with_timeout_sync()
            with self._lock:
                # Re-check in case another thread created one
                if len(self._connections) < self._config.max_size:
                    pooled = _PooledConnection(
                        connection=conn,
                        in_use=True,
                        acquired_at=time.monotonic(),
                    )
                    self._connections.append(pooled)
                else:
                    # Pool filled while we were creating - use as ephemeral
                    ephemeral = conn
                    self._ephemeral_count += 1

        # Helper to release connection on exception
        def _cleanup_on_exception(p: _PooledConnection[ConnT] | None, e: ConnT | None) -> None:
            """Release connection if exception occurs after marking in_use."""
            if p is not None:
                with self._lock:
                    p.in_use = False
                    p.acquired_at = None
            elif e is not None:
                try:
                    e.close()
                except Exception as close_err:
                    logger.warning("Error closing connection on cleanup: %s", close_err)

        try:
            if pooled is not None:
                with self._lock:
                    self._total_acquisitions += 1
                # Record pool checkout time (fast path - found existing connection)
                if checkout_start is not None:
                    checkout_time_ms = (time.monotonic() - checkout_start) * 1000.0
                    _imp_api_l2092_timing_tracking().record_pool_checkout_timing(checkout_time_ms)
                elapsed_ms = (time.monotonic() - acquire_start) * 1000.0
                logger.info(
                    "Connection taken from pool (sync) pool_size=%d available=%d elapsed_ms=%.2f",
                    self.size,
                    self.available,
                    elapsed_ms,
                )
                return pooled.connection
            if ephemeral is not None:
                with self._lock:
                    self._total_acquisitions += 1
                # Record pool checkout time (pool filled while creating)
                if checkout_start is not None:
                    checkout_time_ms = (time.monotonic() - checkout_start) * 1000.0
                    _imp_api_l2092_timing_tracking().record_pool_checkout_timing(checkout_time_ms)
                elapsed_ms = (time.monotonic() - acquire_start) * 1000.0
                logger.info(
                    "Connection taken (sync, ephemeral, pool filled during creation) pool_size=%d elapsed_ms=%.2f",
                    self.size,
                    elapsed_ms,
                )
                return ephemeral
            # All pooled connections in use and at max_size
            # Create ephemeral connection to avoid blocking/deadlock
            logger.debug(
                "Pool exhausted (size=%d, max=%d), creating ephemeral connection (sync)",
                self.size,
                self._config.max_size,
            )
            ephemeral = self._create_connection_with_timeout_sync()
            with self._lock:
                self._ephemeral_count += 1
                self._total_acquisitions += 1
            # Record pool checkout time AFTER ephemeral connection creation
            if checkout_start is not None:
                checkout_time_ms = (time.monotonic() - checkout_start) * 1000.0
                _imp_api_l2092_timing_tracking().record_pool_checkout_timing(checkout_time_ms)
            elapsed_ms = (time.monotonic() - acquire_start) * 1000.0
            logger.info(
                "Connection taken (sync, ephemeral, pool exhausted) pool_size=%d max_size=%d elapsed_ms=%.2f",
                self.size,
                self._config.max_size,
                elapsed_ms,
            )
            return ephemeral
        except Exception:
            # Ensure connection slot is released on any exception
            _cleanup_on_exception(pooled, ephemeral)
            raise

    def _release_sync(self, conn: ConnT) -> None:
        """Synchronously release a connection back to the pool.

        Call this method when done with a connection acquired via
        ``acquire_sync()``. If the connection was pooled, it's returned
        to the pool. If it was ephemeral (created when pool was exhausted),
        it's closed.

        Parameters
        ----------
        conn
            The connection to release (must have been acquired via acquire_sync)

        Note
        ----
        This method is safe to call even if the connection is not from this
        pool - it will simply close the connection.

        Example
        -------
        ::

            conn = pool.acquire_sync()
            try:
                # Use connection...
                pass
            finally:
                pool.release_sync(conn)
        """
        pooled: _PooledConnection[ConnT] | None = None
        acquired_at: float | None = None

        with self._lock:
            # Find the pooled connection wrapper for this connection
            for p in self._connections:
                if p.connection is conn:
                    # Guard against double-release: only process if still in_use
                    if not p.in_use:
                        logger.debug("release_sync called on already-released connection")
                        return
                    pooled = p
                    acquired_at = p.acquired_at
                    break

        if pooled is not None:
            # Check if connection is still alive before returning to pool.
            # Liveness check exceptions are treated as "dead".
            try:
                conn_alive = self._is_connection_alive(conn)
            except db_exc.ProgrammingError:
                self._evict_connection(
                    pooled,
                    "liveness ProgrammingError after sync use",
                )
                raise
            except Exception:
                logger.warning(
                    "Liveness check raised during sync release",
                    exc_info=True,
                )
                self._evict_connection(pooled, "liveness check error after sync use")
                raise
            if not conn_alive:
                self._evict_connection(pooled, "dead after sync use")
                if acquired_at is not None:
                    active_time_ms = (time.monotonic() - acquired_at) * 1000.0
                    logger.info(
                        "Dead connection evicted after sync use active_time_ms=%.2f",
                        active_time_ms,
                    )
            else:
                # Clean up connection state before returning to pool.
                # If cleanup fails, evict instead of returning a corrupt connection.
                try:
                    self._cleanup_connection_state_sync(conn)
                except Exception:
                    self._cleanup_failures += 1
                    logger.warning(
                        "Connection cleanup failed on sync return to pool (cleanup_failures=%d)",
                        self._cleanup_failures,
                        exc_info=True,
                    )
                    self._evict_connection(pooled, "cleanup failed on sync return")
                    if acquired_at is not None:
                        active_time_ms = (time.monotonic() - acquired_at) * 1000.0
                        logger.info(
                            "Connection evicted after sync cleanup failure active_time_ms=%.2f",
                            active_time_ms,
                        )
                    raise
                # Return to pool
                with self._lock:
                    pooled.in_use = False
                    pooled.last_used_at = time.monotonic()
                    pooled.acquired_at = None
                # Calculate active time if we have acquisition timestamp
                if acquired_at is not None:
                    active_time_ms = (time.monotonic() - acquired_at) * 1000.0
                    logger.info(
                        "Connection returned to pool (sync) pool_size=%d available=%d active_time_ms=%.2f",
                        self.size,
                        self.available,
                        active_time_ms,
                    )
                else:
                    logger.info(
                        "Connection returned to pool (sync) pool_size=%d available=%d",
                        self.size,
                        self.available,
                    )
        else:
            # Ephemeral connection - close it
            try:
                conn.close()
                logger.info("Connection closed (sync, ephemeral)")
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning("Error closing ephemeral connection (sync): %s", e)

    def _cleanup_connection_state_sync(self, conn: ConnT) -> None:
        """Clean up connection state synchronously before returning to pool.

        This is the sync equivalent of ``_cleanup_connection_state()``.
        Ensures the connection is not left in an aborted transaction state.

        Raises
        ------
        Exception
            Re-raised from the rollback operation so the caller can decide
            whether to evict the connection.

        Parameters
        ----------
        conn
            The connection to clean up before returning to pool.
        """
        trace_open_state = conn._trace_open_transaction_state
        if callable(trace_open_state):
            trace_open_state(context=DiagnosticLabel("pool-cleanup-sync"))
        consume_backend_closed = getattr(conn, "_consume_data_transaction_backend_closed", None)
        if callable(consume_backend_closed) and consume_backend_closed():
            return
        # Let exceptions propagate so the caller (release_sync) can evict
        # the connection rather than returning it in a broken state.
        rollback_fn = conn._rollback
        if callable(rollback_fn):
            # Use recreate_cursor=True to ensure cursor is in clean state
            rollback_fn(recreate_cursor=True)

    @contextmanager
    def _acquire_sync_context(self) -> Generator[ConnT]:
        """Context manager for synchronous connection acquisition.

        Automatically releases the connection when the context exits,
        even if an exception is raised.

        Thread affinity checks are automatically disabled for the duration
        of the context because pooled connections may have been created in a
        different thread (e.g., during warmup).  The pool guarantees that
        only one caller uses a connection at a time, so this is safe.

        Yields
        ------
        ConnT
            A database connection ready for use

        Example
        -------
        ::

            # In async code using an application-owned thread pool
            async def run_query():
                def sync_work():
                    with pool.acquire_sync_context() as conn:
                        session = conn.session(SessionId.system())
                        return session.read(lambda txn: txn.query(Model).execute())
                return await run_sync_in_worker(sync_work)
        """
        conn = self._acquire_sync()
        try:
            with _imp_api_l2050_transaction().disable_thread_affinity_checks():
                yield conn
        finally:
            self._release_sync(conn)

    def _initialize_sync(self) -> None:
        """Synchronously initialize the pool (blocking warmup).

        This method blocks until warmup completes. Use this when you need
        the pool to be ready before proceeding (e.g., during app startup
        in sync code).

        For async code, use ``await pool.initialize()`` instead.

        Note
        ----
        This method always performs blocking warmup, regardless of the
        ``warmup_in_background`` config setting.
        """
        if self._initialized:
            return

        with self._lock:
            if self._initialized:
                return

            self._initialized = True
            self._shutdown = False

            # Log connection string with password redacted for debugging
            redacted_conn_str = self._redact_connection_string(self._config.connection_string)
            logger.info(
                "Connection pool initializing sync (min=%d, max=%d, connection=%s)",
                self._config.min_size,
                self._config.max_size,
                redacted_conn_str,
            )

        # Warmup pool synchronously (always blocking for sync init)
        if self._config.warmup_on_init:
            self._warmup_pool_sync()

    def _warmup_pool_sync(self) -> None:
        """Fill pool to min_size synchronously.

        Creates connections one at a time (no batching) since we're in
        sync context and can't parallelize without threads.
        """
        self._warmup_in_progress = True
        try:
            with self._lock:
                current_size = len(self._connections)
            needed = self._config.min_size - current_size

            if needed <= 0:
                logger.debug("Pool warmup sync: already at min_size (%d)", current_size)
                self._warmup_completed_at = WarmupCompletionTime(time.monotonic())
                return

            logger.info(
                "Pool warmup sync starting: creating %d connections",
                needed,
            )

            # Create connections one at a time with DNS resolution and timeout
            for _ in range(needed):
                if self._shutdown:
                    logger.info("Pool warmup sync cancelled due to shutdown")
                    break

                try:
                    conn = self._create_connection_with_timeout_sync()
                    close_excess = False
                    with self._lock:
                        # Respect max_size even during warmup (defensive check)
                        if len(self._connections) >= self._config.max_size:
                            close_excess = True
                            logger.debug("Pool at max_size, closing warmup connection")
                        else:
                            self._warmup_connections_created += 1
                            pooled: _PooledConnection[ConnT] = _PooledConnection(
                                connection=conn,
                            )
                            self._connections.append(pooled)

                    # Close excess connection OUTSIDE the lock (may do I/O)
                    if close_excess:
                        try:
                            conn.close()
                        except Exception as e:
                            logger.debug("Error closing excess warmup connection (sync): %s", e)
                        continue
                except Exception as e:
                    with self._lock:
                        self._warmup_connections_failed += 1
                    logger.warning(
                        "Failed to create warmup connection (sync): %s",
                        e,
                    )

            self._warmup_completed_at = WarmupCompletionTime(time.monotonic())
            logger.info(
                "Pool warmup sync complete: %d connections created, %d failed, pool size=%d",
                self._warmup_connections_created,
                self._warmup_connections_failed,
                len(self._connections),
            )

        finally:
            self._warmup_in_progress = False

    def _close_sync(self) -> None:
        """Synchronously close all connections in the pool.

        This is the sync equivalent of ``close()``. Use this when shutting
        down from sync code.

        Note: This does NOT cancel async background tasks (warmup, maintenance).
        For full cleanup in async code, use ``await pool.close()`` instead.

        After calling this method, the pool cannot be used until
        ``initialize()`` or ``initialize_sync()`` is called again.
        """
        self._shutdown = True

        # Clean up shared executor
        if self._sync_executor is not None:
            self._sync_executor.shutdown(wait=False)
            self._sync_executor = None

        # Snapshot and clear under the lock, close OUTSIDE the lock.
        with self._lock:
            connections_to_close = list(self._connections)
            closed_count = len(self._connections)
            self._connections.clear()
            self._initialized = False

        for pooled in connections_to_close:
            try:
                pooled.connection.close()
                logger.info("Connection closed (sync, pool shutdown)")
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning("Error closing pooled connection (sync): %s", e)

        logger.info(
            "Connection pool closed (sync): %d connections closed, %d ephemeral connections were created during lifetime",
            closed_count,
            self._ephemeral_count,
        )

    async def _close_async(self) -> None:
        """Close all connections in the pool.

        This should be called during application shutdown. Stops background
        tasks and closes all connections.

        Note: The global DNS cache is NOT stopped - it's shared across all
        pools and only reset during application shutdown via ``reset_dns_cache()``.

        After calling this method, the pool cannot be used until
        ``initialize()`` is called again.
        """
        self._shutdown = True

        # Cancel background tasks
        if self._warmup_task is not None:
            await _cancel_pool_background_task(self._warmup_task)
            self._warmup_task = None

        if self._maintenance_task is not None:
            await _cancel_pool_background_task(self._maintenance_task)
            self._maintenance_task = None

        # Clean up shared executor
        if self._sync_executor is not None:
            self._sync_executor.shutdown(wait=False)
            self._sync_executor = None

        # Snapshot and clear connections under the lock, then close OUTSIDE
        # the lock.  close_async() may do I/O (e.g., PostgreSQL DISCARD ALL)
        # and must not block concurrent pool operations.
        with self._lock:
            connections_to_close = list(self._connections)
            closed_count = len(self._connections)
            self._connections.clear()
            self._initialized = False

        for pooled in connections_to_close:
            try:
                # Use async close to properly close both sync and async connections
                # (e.g., aiosqlite worker threads)
                await pooled.connection.close_async()
                logger.info("Connection closed (pool shutdown)")
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning("Error closing pooled connection: %s", e)

        logger.info(
            "Connection pool closed: %d connections closed, %d ephemeral connections were created during lifetime",
            closed_count,
            self._ephemeral_count,
        )

    @property
    def size(self) -> int:
        """Current number of connections in pool."""
        return len(self._connections)

    @property
    def available(self) -> int:
        """Number of available (not in use) connections."""
        return sum(1 for p in self._connections if not p.in_use)

    @property
    def in_use(self) -> int:
        """Number of connections currently in use."""
        return sum(1 for p in self._connections if p.in_use)

    @property
    def is_initialized(self) -> bool:
        """Whether the pool has been initialized."""
        return self._initialized

    async def _create_notification_channel_async(
        self,
        session_id: SessionId | None = None,
    ) -> NotificationChannel:
        """Create a notification channel for cross-process signaling.

        Creates a **dedicated** database connection (outside the pool) and
        wraps it in a :class:`~l2200_notification.NotificationChannel`
        implementation appropriate for the current backend:

        * **PostgreSQL**: Uses LISTEN/NOTIFY (~1ms latency)
        * **Other backends**: Uses polling via ``sys_notifications`` table (~25-75ms)

        The returned channel owns its connection and must be closed when
        no longer needed (via ``await channel.close()``).

        Parameters
        ----------
        session_id
            Session ID for database operations. Required for polling backends.
        Returns
        -------
        NotificationChannel
            A notification channel ready for subscribe/notify operations.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If ``session_id`` is required (polling backend) but not provided.

        Example
        -------
        ::

            channel = await pool.create_notification_channel(session_id=service_session_id)
            async with channel:
                await channel.subscribe("ipc:commands")
                async for notification in channel.notifications():
                    handle(notification)

        See Also
        --------
        :mod:`l2200_notification` : Notification channel module
        :func:`l2200_notification.create_notification_channel` : Factory function
        """
        backend_capability_cls = _imp_api_l1200_capabilities().BackendCapability
        create_notification_channel = _imp_api_l2200_notification().create_notification_channel

        # Complete bootstrap on the pool's first connection before a dedicated
        # connection can bootstrap the same physical database.
        warmup_task = getattr(self, "_warmup_task", None)
        if warmup_task is not None:
            await asyncio.shield(warmup_task)

        # Create a dedicated connection for the notification channel.
        # This connection is NOT managed by the pool — the caller (or the
        # channel itself) is responsible for its lifecycle.
        dedicated_conn = await self._create_connection_async()

        # Get capabilities from the dedicated connection
        capabilities = frozenset(dedicated_conn.get_capabilities())

        # For PostgreSQL, the factory creates its own async connection from
        # the connection string, so the dedicated_conn is only used to
        # extract capabilities. For polling/filewatch, the dedicated_conn
        # is used directly by the channel.
        has_realtime = backend_capability_cls.REALTIME_NOTIFY in capabilities
        try:
            channel = await create_notification_channel(
                dedicated_conn,
                capabilities,
                session_id=session_id,
                connection_string=self._config.connection_string,
                # For non-realtime backends the channel owns and will close
                # the dedicated connection. For PostgreSQL the factory creates
                # its own async connection; we close dedicated_conn below.
                owns_connection=not has_realtime,
            )
        except BaseException:
            # If the factory fails, close the dedicated connection to prevent
            # a leak regardless of backend type.
            await dedicated_conn.close_async()
            raise

        # For realtime (PostgreSQL) backends, the factory creates its own
        # connection and dedicated_conn was only needed for capability
        # detection. Close it to avoid a leak.
        if has_realtime:
            await dedicated_conn.close_async()

        logger.info(
            "Created notification channel via pool (backend=%s)",
            "realtime" if has_realtime else "polling",
        )
        return cast("NotificationChannel", channel)

    def stats(self) -> PoolStats:
        """Get pool statistics for monitoring.

        Returns
        -------
        PoolStats
            Current pool statistics including size, usage, warmup, and DNS stats
        """
        # Get DNS cache stats if enabled (from global singleton)
        dns_hits = 0
        dns_misses = 0
        dns_avg_ms = 0.0
        if self._dns_cache_enabled:
            dns_cache = _imp_api_l2000_connection_dns_cache().get_dns_cache()
            dns_stats = dns_cache.stats()
            dns_hits = dns_stats.cache_hits
            dns_misses = dns_stats.cache_misses
            dns_avg_ms = dns_stats.avg_resolution_time_ms

        # Calculate average connection time
        avg_conn_ms = 0.0
        if self._connection_count > 0:
            avg_conn_ms = self._total_connection_time_ms / self._connection_count

        # Read size/available/in_use under a single lock acquisition to ensure
        # a consistent snapshot (otherwise size != available + in_use is possible
        # when connections are acquired or released between property reads).
        with self._lock:
            snap_size = len(self._connections)
            snap_available = sum(1 for p in self._connections if not p.in_use)
            snap_in_use = sum(1 for p in self._connections if p.in_use)

        return PoolStats(
            size=snap_size,
            available=snap_available,
            in_use=snap_in_use,
            min_size=self._config.min_size,
            max_size=self._config.max_size,
            ephemeral_created=self._ephemeral_count,
            total_acquisitions=self._total_acquisitions,
            # Warmup stats
            warmup_connections_created=self._warmup_connections_created,
            warmup_connections_failed=self._warmup_connections_failed,
            warmup_in_progress=self._warmup_in_progress,
            warmup_completed_at=self._warmup_completed_at,
            # DNS stats
            dns_cache_hits=dns_hits,
            dns_cache_misses=dns_misses,
            dns_avg_resolution_ms=dns_avg_ms,
            # Connection timing
            avg_connection_time_ms=avg_conn_ms,
            max_connection_time_ms=self._max_connection_time_ms,
            # Connection health
            dead_connections_evicted=self._dead_connections_evicted,
            idle_connections_evicted=self._idle_connections_evicted,
        )


class AsyncConnectionPool[ConnT: "_DatabaseConnectionCore"](_ConnectionPoolBase[ConnT]):
    """Connection pool that creates and serves only async-owned connections."""

    async def _create_connection(self) -> ConnT:
        """Create an async-owned connection for this pool."""
        return await self._create_connection_async()

    async def initialize(self) -> None:
        """Initialize the pool using async connection creation."""
        await self._initialize_async()

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def acquire(self) -> AsyncGenerator[ConnT]:
        """Acquire an async-owned connection."""
        async with self._acquire_async() as conn:
            yield conn

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the async pool and its connections."""
        await self._close_async()

    async def create_notification_channel(
        self,
        session_id: SessionId | None = None,
    ) -> NotificationChannel:
        """Create a notification channel using an async-created dedicated connection."""
        return await self._create_notification_channel_async(session_id=session_id)

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def notification_channel_context(
        self,
        *,
        session_id: SessionId,
    ) -> AsyncGenerator[NotificationChannel]:
        """Own one dedicated notification channel for the context lifetime."""
        channel = await self._create_notification_channel_async(session_id=session_id)
        try:
            yield channel
        finally:
            await channel.close()


class SyncConnectionPool[ConnT: "_DatabaseConnectionCore"](_ConnectionPoolBase[ConnT]):
    """Connection pool that creates and serves only sync-owned connections."""

    def initialize(self) -> None:
        """Initialize the pool using sync connection creation."""
        self._initialize_sync()

    def acquire(self) -> ConnT:
        """Acquire a sync-owned connection."""
        return self._acquire_sync()

    def release(self, conn: ConnT) -> None:
        """Release a sync-owned connection back to the pool."""
        self._release_sync(conn)

    @contextmanager
    def acquire_context(self) -> Generator[ConnT]:
        """Acquire a sync-owned connection in a context manager."""
        with self._acquire_sync_context() as conn:
            yield conn

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the sync pool and its connections."""
        self._close_sync()


# =============================================================================
# Pool Registry
# =============================================================================


class PoolName(str):
    """Stable identity of a registered connection pool."""


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class NoRegisteredPool:
    """Explicit absence of a pool under a registry name."""


NO_REGISTERED_POOL = NoRegisteredPool()
type RegisteredPool = ConnectionPoolMetricsProvider | NoRegisteredPool


class RegisteredPoolSnapshot(Mapping[PoolName, ConnectionPoolMetricsProvider]):
    """Immutable snapshot of all registry entries."""

    __slots__ = ("_entries",)

    def __init__(
        self: RegisteredPoolSnapshot,
        entries: tuple[tuple[PoolName, ConnectionPoolMetricsProvider], ...],
    ) -> None:
        self._entries = dict(entries)

    def __getitem__(self: RegisteredPoolSnapshot, name: PoolName) -> ConnectionPoolMetricsProvider:
        return self._entries[name]

    def __iter__(self: RegisteredPoolSnapshot) -> Iterator[PoolName]:
        return iter(self._entries)

    def __len__(self: RegisteredPoolSnapshot) -> int:
        return len(self._entries)


class _PoolRegistryEntries:
    """Lock-protected registry storage owner."""

    __slots__ = ("_entries",)

    def __init__(self: _PoolRegistryEntries) -> None:
        self._entries = dict[PoolName, ConnectionPoolMetricsProvider]()

    def register(
        self: _PoolRegistryEntries,
        name: PoolName,
        pool: ConnectionPoolMetricsProvider,
    ) -> None:
        self._entries[name] = pool

    def unregister(self: _PoolRegistryEntries, name: PoolName) -> bool:
        return self._entries.pop(name, None) is not None

    def get(self: _PoolRegistryEntries, name: PoolName) -> RegisteredPool:
        return self._entries.get(name, NO_REGISTERED_POOL)

    def snapshot(self: _PoolRegistryEntries) -> RegisteredPoolSnapshot:
        return RegisteredPoolSnapshot(tuple(self._entries.items()))

    def clear(self: _PoolRegistryEntries) -> None:
        self._entries.clear()


class PoolRegistry:
    """Registry for managing connection pool instances.

    Provides a central place to register and retrieve connection pools
    by name, enabling admin tools and monitoring to access pools without
    passing them explicitly.

    Thread Safety
    -------------
    All operations are protected by a class-level lock for thread-safe access.

    Example
    -------
    ::

        # Register a pool during application startup
        pool = AsyncConnectionPool(config)
        await pool.initialize()
        PoolRegistry.register("default", pool)

        # Later, access from admin tools
        pool = PoolRegistry.get("default")
        stats = pool.stats()

        # Or get all pools
        for name, pool in PoolRegistry.get_all().items():
            print(f"{name}: {pool.stats()}")
    """

    _pools: ClassVar[_PoolRegistryEntries] = _PoolRegistryEntries()
    _lock: ClassVar[threading.Lock] = threading.Lock()

    @classmethod
    def register(
        cls,
        name: PoolName,
        pool: ConnectionPoolMetricsProvider,
    ) -> None:
        """Register a pool with a name.

        Parameters
        ----------
        name
            Unique name for this pool (e.g., "default", "read-replica")
        pool
            The connection pool instance
        """
        with cls._lock:
            cls._pools.register(name, pool)
        logger.debug("Registered connection pool: %s", name)

    @classmethod
    def unregister(cls, name: PoolName) -> None:
        """Unregister a pool by name.

        Parameters
        ----------
        name
            Name of the pool to remove
        """
        with cls._lock:
            if cls._pools.unregister(name):
                logger.debug("Unregistered connection pool: %s", name)

    @classmethod
    def get(
        cls,
        name: PoolName = PoolName("default"),
    ) -> RegisteredPool:
        """Get a pool by name.

        Parameters
        ----------
        name
            Name of the pool (default: "default")

        Returns
        -------
        connection pool metrics provider | None
            The pool if found, None otherwise
        """
        with cls._lock:
            return cls._pools.get(name)

    @classmethod
    def get_all(cls) -> RegisteredPoolSnapshot:
        """Get all registered pools.

        RegisteredPoolSnapshot
            Immutable pool-name-to-provider snapshot.
        """
        with cls._lock:
            return cls._pools.snapshot()

    @classmethod
    def clear(cls) -> None:
        """Clear all registered pools (for testing)."""
        with cls._lock:
            cls._pools.clear()


# =============================================================================
# Metrics Functions
# =============================================================================
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class NoPoolMetrics:
    """Explicit absence of metrics for an unregistered pool."""


NO_POOL_METRICS = NoPoolMetrics()


@dataclass
class PoolMetrics:
    """Metrics snapshot for a connection pool.

    Provides comprehensive visibility into pool health and performance.
    Collected at a point in time via ``get_pool_metrics()``.

    Attributes
    ----------
    pool_name
        Name of the pool in the registry
    timestamp
        When these metrics were collected
    size
        Current number of connections in the pool
    available
        Number of connections available for checkout
    in_use
        Number of connections currently in use
    min_size
        Configured minimum pool size
    max_size
        Configured maximum pool size
    ephemeral_created
        Total ephemeral connections created (indicates pool exhaustion)
    total_acquisitions
        Total number of connection acquisitions
    is_healthy
        Whether the pool is healthy (no ephemeral connections)
    utilization_ratio
        Ratio of in-use to total connections
    ephemeral_ratio
        Ratio of ephemeral to total acquisitions

    Example
    -------
    ::

        metrics = get_pool_metrics("default")
        print(f"Pool: {metrics.available}/{metrics.size} available")
        print(f"Utilization: {metrics.utilization_ratio:.1%}")
        if not metrics.is_healthy:
            print(f"Warning: {metrics.ephemeral_created} ephemeral connections")
    """

    pool_name: PoolName
    timestamp: float

    # Size metrics
    size: int
    available: int
    in_use: int
    min_size: int
    max_size: int

    # Acquisition metrics
    ephemeral_created: int
    total_acquisitions: int

    # Computed health indicators
    is_healthy: bool
    utilization_ratio: float
    ephemeral_ratio: float


def get_pool_metrics(
    pool_name: PoolName = PoolName("default"),
) -> PoolMetrics | NoPoolMetrics:
    """Get metrics for a registered connection pool.

    Parameters
    ----------
    pool_name
        Name of the pool to query (default: "default")

    Returns
    -------
    PoolMetrics | NoPoolMetrics
        Metrics snapshot if the pool exists, or explicit absence otherwise

    Example
    -------
    ::

        metrics = get_pool_metrics(PoolName("default"))
        if isinstance(metrics, PoolMetrics):
            print(f"Pool utilization: {metrics.utilization_ratio:.1%}")
            if not metrics.is_healthy:
                print("Warning: Pool is exhausted, consider increasing max_size")
    """
    pool = PoolRegistry.get(pool_name)
    if isinstance(pool, NoRegisteredPool):
        return NO_POOL_METRICS

    stats = pool.stats()
    return PoolMetrics(
        pool_name=pool_name,
        timestamp=time.time(),
        size=stats.size,
        available=stats.available,
        in_use=stats.in_use,
        min_size=stats.min_size,
        max_size=stats.max_size,
        ephemeral_created=stats.ephemeral_created,
        total_acquisitions=stats.total_acquisitions,
        is_healthy=stats.is_healthy,
        utilization_ratio=stats.utilization_ratio,
        ephemeral_ratio=stats.ephemeral_ratio,
    )


def get_all_pool_metrics() -> tuple[PoolMetrics, ...]:
    """Get metrics for all registered connection pools.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[PoolMetrics, ...]
        Metrics for each registered pool

    Example
    -------
    ::

        all_metrics = get_all_pool_metrics()
        for metrics in all_metrics:
            print(f"{metrics.pool_name}: {metrics.size} connections")
            if not metrics.is_healthy:
                print(f"  Warning: {metrics.pool_name} is unhealthy!")
    """
    results = []
    for name in sorted(PoolRegistry.get_all().keys()):
        metrics = get_pool_metrics(name)
        if isinstance(metrics, PoolMetrics):
            results.append(metrics)
    return tuple(results)


__all__ = [
    "AsyncConnectionPool",
    "ConnectionPoolMetricsProvider",
    "ConnectionPoolConfig",
    "NoPoolMetrics",
    "PoolMetrics",
    "PoolRegistry",
    "PoolStats",
    "SyncConnectionPool",
    "get_all_pool_metrics",
    "get_pool_metrics",
]

from __future__ import annotations

import abc

from dataclasses import replace
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

    from impl.common.l2050_sql_types.sql_branded_types import SqlTableName

class SchemaReconciliationOwner(abc.ABC):
    """Concrete base contract for observe-then-build schema transactions."""

    def build_schema_reconciliation_interrogation_request(
        self,
        models: Sequence[type[DatabaseObjectRow[SysId]]],
    ) -> SchemaReconciliationInterrogationRequest:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def _declare_versioned_log_models_for_planning(
        self,
        model_classes: tuple[type[VersionedObjectRow[SysId]], ...],
        *,
        enable_logging: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        """Publish immutable log-model declarations before planning."""
        del model_classes, enable_logging

    def build_versioned_schema_reconciliation_interrogation_request(
        self,
        model_classes: Sequence[type[VersionedObjectRow[SysId]]],

@external_io_boundary
def observe_schema_reconciliation_state(
    txn: SchemaReconciliationOwner,
    request: SchemaReconciliationInterrogationRequest,
) -> SchemaStateSnapshot:
    """Observe the catalog and probe data-dependent column additions."""
    from l3200_metadata.schema_state_snapshot import (
        SchemaFactSource,
        SchemaReconciliationInterrogationRequest,
        SchemaTableFact,
    )

    snapshot = resolve_terminal_sync(
        txn,
        "schema_reconciliation_coordinator.observe",
        txn.interrogate_schema_reconciliation_state_lazy(request),
    )
    observed_table_names = {fact.table_name for fact in snapshot.table_facts}
    missing_table_facts = tuple(
        SchemaTableFact(
            table_name=table_name,
            exists=False,
            source=SchemaFactSource.RECONCILIATION_OBSERVATION,
        )
        for table_name in request.table_names
        if table_name not in observed_table_names
    )
    if missing_table_facts:
        snapshot = replace(snapshot, table_facts=(*snapshot.table_facts, *missing_table_facts))
    probe_table_names: list[SqlTableName] = []
    for table_name, column_names in request.required_columns_by_table:
        if snapshot.table_exists(table_name) is not True:
            continue
        observed_columns = snapshot.columns_for_table(table_name)
        if any(column not in observed_columns for column in column_names):
            probe_table_names.append(table_name)
    probe_tables = tuple(dict.fromkeys(probe_table_names))
    if probe_tables:
        row_snapshot = resolve_terminal_sync(
            txn,
            "schema_reconciliation_coordinator.observe_rows",
            txn.interrogate_schema_reconciliation_state_lazy(
                SchemaReconciliationInterrogationRequest(
                    table_names=probe_tables,
                    row_presence_only=True,
                ),
            ),
        )
        row_presence = {fact.table_name: fact.row_presence for fact in row_snapshot.table_facts}
        if any(row_presence.get(table_name, SchemaFactPresence.UNKNOWN) is SchemaFactPresence.UNKNOWN for table_name in probe_tables):
            raise ValueError("Schema reconciliation requires complete row-presence observations")
        snapshot = replace(
            snapshot,
            table_facts=tuple(
                replace(fact, row_presence=row_presence.get(fact.table_name, fact.row_presence)) for fact in snapshot.table_facts
            ),
        )
    return snapshot


@external_io_boundary
def create_tables_from_schema_with_reconciliation(
    txn: SchemaReconciliationOwner,
    model_classes: Sequence[type[DatabaseObjectRow[SysId]]],
    *,
    if_not_exists: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Observe scoped facts and enqueue a closed set of table reconciliations."""
    model_classes = tuple(model_classes)
    if not model_classes:
        return
    request = txn.build_schema_reconciliation_interrogation_request(model_classes)
    snapshot = observe_schema_reconciliation_state(txn, request)
    with txn._schema_reconciliation_snapshot_scope(snapshot):
        create_and_flush = getattr(txn, "_create_table_from_schema_and_flush_lazy", None)
        if not callable(create_and_flush):
            msg = "Schema reconciliation owner does not provide table creation and flush"
            raise TypeError(msg)
        for model_cls in model_classes:
            create_and_flush(
                model_cls,
                if_not_exists=if_not_exists,
            )


@external_io_boundary
def create_table_from_schema_with_reconciliation(
    txn: SchemaReconciliationOwner,
    model_cls: type[DatabaseObjectRow[SysId]],
    *,
    if_not_exists: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Observe physical state, build against the immutable snapshot, then execute."""
    create_tables_from_schema_with_reconciliation(
        txn,
        (model_cls,),
        if_not_exists=if_not_exists,
    )


@external_io_boundary
def create_versioned_table_with_reconciliation(
    txn: SchemaReconciliationOwner,
    model_cls: type[VersionedObjectRow[SysId]],
    *,
    enable_logging: bool = True,
    if_not_exists: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Observe one complete versioned family before planning schema evolution."""
    create_versioned_tables_with_reconciliation(
        txn,
        (model_cls,),
        enable_logging=enable_logging,
        if_not_exists=if_not_exists,
    )


@external_io_boundary
def create_versioned_tables_with_reconciliation(
    txn: SchemaReconciliationOwner,
    model_classes: Sequence[type[VersionedObjectRow[SysId]]],
    *,
    enable_logging: bool = True,
    if_not_exists: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Observe versioned physical families before planning their reconciliation."""
    model_classes = tuple(model_classes)
    if not model_classes:
        return
    txn._declare_versioned_log_models_for_planning(
        model_classes,
        enable_logging=enable_logging,
    )
    request = txn.build_versioned_schema_reconciliation_interrogation_request(
        model_classes,
        enable_logging=enable_logging,
    )
    snapshot = observe_schema_reconciliation_state(txn, request)
    with txn._schema_reconciliation_snapshot_scope(snapshot):
        for model_cls in model_classes:
            resolve_terminal_sync(
                txn,
                "schema_reconciliation_coordinator.create_versioned",
                txn.create_versioned_table_lazy(
                    model_cls,
                    enable_logging=enable_logging,
                    if_not_exists=if_not_exists,
                ),
            )


@external_io_boundary
async def create_versioned_table_with_reconciliation_async(
    txn: SchemaReconciliationOwner,
    model_cls: type[VersionedObjectRow[SysId]],
    *,
    enable_logging: bool = True,
    if_not_exists: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Async observe-then-plan boundary for one complete versioned family."""
    txn._declare_versioned_log_models_for_planning(
        (model_cls,),
        enable_logging=enable_logging,
    )
    request = txn.build_versioned_schema_reconciliation_interrogation_request(
        (model_cls,),
        enable_logging=enable_logging,
    )
    snapshot = await txn.interrogate_schema_reconciliation_state_lazy(request)
    with txn._schema_reconciliation_snapshot_scope(snapshot):
        await txn.create_versioned_table_lazy(
            model_cls,
            enable_logging=enable_logging,
            if_not_exists=if_not_exists,
        )


@external_io_boundary
def reconcile_schema_models(
    txn: SchemaReconciliationOwner,
    model_classes: Sequence[type[DatabaseObjectRow[SysId]]],
) -> None:
    """Observe once and execute one reconciliation plan for ``model_classes``."""
    model_classes = tuple(model_classes)
    if not model_classes:
        return
    request = txn.build_schema_reconciliation_interrogation_request(model_classes)
    snapshot = observe_schema_reconciliation_state(txn, request)
    with txn._schema_reconciliation_snapshot_scope(snapshot):
        result = txn.build_reconciliation_plan_lazy(snapshot, model_classes)
        resolve_terminal_sync(txn, "schema_reconciliation_coordinator.reconcile", result)


@external_io_boundary
async def reconcile_schema_models_async(
    txn: SchemaReconciliationOwner,
    model_classes: Sequence[type[DatabaseObjectRow[SysId]]],
) -> None:
    """Async observe-once reconciliation for ``model_classes``."""
    model_classes = tuple(model_classes)
    if not model_classes:
        return
    request = txn.build_schema_reconciliation_interrogation_request(model_classes)
    snapshot_result = txn.interrogate_schema_reconciliation_state_lazy(request)
    snapshot = await snapshot_result
    with txn._schema_reconciliation_snapshot_scope(snapshot):
        result = txn.build_reconciliation_plan_lazy(snapshot, model_classes)
        await result
